Scoopable Cookies

Is this the best trend ever?

Serves 10Prep 5 minCook 12 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened (113 g, 1 stick)
  • 3/4 cup tightly packed brown sugar (I like using 1/2 cup light brown and 1/4 cup dark brown, but you can use either or) (150 g total)
  • 1/4 cup white sugar (50 g)
  • 1 egg, room temperature
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1 3/4 cup all purpose flour (220 g)
  • 3/4 tsp baking soda
  • 1/4 tsp salt
  • 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips or chunks
  • flaky salt for topping, optional
  • vanilla ice cream for serving
  • chocolate or caramel sauce, optional

Steps

  1. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, or a handheld mixer, cream together butter, brown sugar, and white sugar for 5 minutes on medium speed until light and fluffy.
  2. Once five minutes is over, add in egg and vanilla and mix until combined.
  3. In a separate bowl, mix flour, baking soda, and salt, and mix until combined. Add these dry ingredients to the butter mixture on low speed, and mix until just combined. Add the chocolate chips or chunks and mix on low until just combined.
  4. Roll out the cookies into big 3 inch sized cookie dough balls, and place on a baking sheet in the freezer for 20 minutes until hard and set. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 350 F (180C).
  5. Place the dough balls close to each other in a deep pan (8x8 or 9x9 inch), nearly touching. Bake 9-12 minutes until golden brown on the edges and soft and gooey in the center.
  6. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt, then scoop out servings using an ice cream scoop while still warm, topping with chocolate sauce, salted caramel, vanilla ice cream, anything you like!

  2. In a large bowl add the ground beef, diced onion, cilantro, spices and salt. Mix well with your hands until combined. Set aside.
  3. Take a tortilla, and then a small ball of meat and place that in the center of the tortilla, then spread the meat evenly from edge to edge. Sprinkle a good amount of cheddar cheese in the center then fold the tortilla over to create a taco.
  4. Place the tacos on a wire rack set inside a baking sheet, making sure not to overlap them. Spray with a little avocado oil and add a little salt and pepper.
  5. Bake for 20-30 minutes til golden and crispy. Remove from oven and let cool on wire rack for 5 minutes.
  6. While they bake prep the avocado sauce by putting all the ingredients into a food processor or blender, and blend until smooth.
  7. Enjoy with the avocado sauce and a squeeze of lime.

Ingredients

  • 2 ½ lb beef pot roast or chuck roast (trimmed and cut into 2-3 large pieces*)
  • 1 ½ cups yellow onion (chopped, plus more for garnish)
  • 4 large garlic cloves (smashed)
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 teaspoon onion powder
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano (mexican oregano if you can find it, it is more citrusy)
  • 1 teaspoons cumin
  • 2 teaspoons chili powder blend
  • ½ teaspoon cinnamon (or 1 small cinnamon stick)
  • 3 ounces chipotle in adobo (see notes)
  • 1 cup canned crushed tomatoes (fire roasted if you can find it)
  • 3 cups beef broth
  • 1 tablespoon white vinegar
  • 2 teaspoons kosher salt
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 16 corn tortillas
  • 2 cups shredded Monterey jack (Oaxaca or queso chihuahua)
  • ½ cup chopped fresh cilantro (for serving)
  • lime wedges (optional for serving)
  • guajillo, ancho and arbol chiles (optional in place of chipotle for a more traditional birria. See note below.)

Steps

  1. Heat a large skillet over medium heat and spray with cooking spray. Brown the beef on all sides in two batches. Transfer the beef to the slow cooker.
  2. In a blender, or food processor, blend 1 cup onion, garlic, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, cumin, chili powder, cinnamon, chipotle in adobo, crushed tomato, beef broth, white vinegar and salt. Pour over beef. Add bay leaves and cook on low heat for 8 hours.
  3. Shred beef strain the broth. Return beef to slow cooker with ½ cup broth and keep warm. Save remaining broth for dipping tortillas and serving.
  4. Quickly dip tortilla in the consommé (broth) and add to a hot skillet or griddle.
  5. Add 3 tablespoons of shredded beef and 2 tablespoons shredded cheese to the tortilla with some onion and cilantro. Fold and cook like a quesadilla until browned on each side.
  6. Serve birria tacos with raw chopped onion and cilantro, plus remaining consommé in a small bowl, for dipping.

Slow Cooker Pot Roast

This slow cooker pot roast is an easy and delicious dinner that's easily made in a slow cooker or crockpot. This version is paleo, whole30, and AIP-friendly.

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 480 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp avocado oil
  • 3 lb boneless beef chuck roast boneless
  • 1 tsp salt (divided)
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • 4 cloves garlic (minced)
  • 1/2 yellow onion (diced)
  • 2 cups carrots (peeled and chopped)
  • 2 cups parsnip (peeled and chopped)
  • 1 tbsp rosemary leaves (chopped)
  • 2 tsp fresh thyme leaves
  • 3 bay leaves
  • 1 3/4 cups beef broth
  • 2 tbsp coconut aminos
  • 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar
  • 1 tbsp arrowroot starch
  • 2 tbsp parsley (chopped)

Steps

  1. Using a large pan, heat the avocado oil over medium heat. Add the roast, season with salt and pepper, and sear for 2-3 minutes on each side or until lightly browned. Remove from the pan and place on the bottom of the slow cooker.
  2. Add the onion and garlic to the pan and saute for 3-4 minutes or until slightly translucent. Remove from the pan and add to the slow cooker.
  3. Add the parsnip, carrots, rosemary, thyme, bay leaves, broth, coconut aminos, and balsamic vinegar to the slow cooker. Place the lid on the slow cooker and cook on low for 7 hours.
  4. Once finished, whisk in the arrowroot starch with about a tablespoon of water until fully combined. Add back to the slow cooker and allow to cook for another hour.
  5. Turn off the slow cooker and remove the bay leaves.
  6. Serve the roasted shredded along with the vegetables and top with several spoonfuls of the broth. Top with chopped parsley.

Slow-Roasted Sticky Balsamic Beef

Slow-Roasted Sticky Balsamic Beef

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • Beef: 3 lbs beef chuck roast (whole or large chunks)
  • Aromatics: 1 large onion (quartered), 4 cloves garlic (smashed)
  • Balsamic Glaze:
  • 3/4 cup balsamic vinegar
  • 1/2 cup brown sugar or honey
  • 1/4 cup soy sauce
  • 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 tbsp Dijon mustard
  • 1 tsp dried thyme
  • Cooking Liquid: 1 cup beef broth
  • Seasoning: Salt and cracked black pepper to taste

Steps

  1. Prep and Sear: Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C). Pat the beef dry, season generously with salt and pepper, and sear in a hot, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven until browned on all sides.
  2. Combine Glaze: In a bowl, whisk together the balsamic vinegar, brown sugar/honey, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard, and thyme.
  3. Slow Roast: Place the onion and garlic around the beef. Pour the balsamic mixture and beef broth over the meat. Cover tightly with a lid or heavy-duty foil.
  4. Cook: Roast in the oven for 3–4 hours, basting the beef with the pan juices every hour, until it is fork-tender and pulls apart easily.
  5. Glaze and Caramelize: Remove the lid for the final 20–30 minutes of cooking. If the sauce hasn’t thickened into a sticky syrup, remove the beef, place the pan over high heat on the stove, and reduce the remaining liquid until it coats the back of a spoon.
  6. Serve: Shred the beef slightly or serve in large, tender chunks, drizzled with the thickened balsamic glaze. Serve over creamy mashed potatoes, polenta, or roasted root vegetables.

Ingredients

  • A buttery sour cream vanilla sheet cake (think sugar cookie vibes… but better) topped with the dreamiest fresh strawberry frosting. It’s sweet but not too sweet, and the frosting is the real star.
  • Sour Cream Vanilla Cake
  • Sheet Pan Size (18 x 13):
  • 2 1/4 sticks (18 Tbsp) butter, room temp
  • 2 1/2 cups sugar
  • 3 large eggs
  • 2 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
  • 3/4 cup milk
  • 1 cup sour cream
  • 3 cups all-purpose flour
  • 3 tsp baking powder
  • 1 tsp sea or kosher salt
  • 9x13 Pan (or Two 8-Inch Rounds):
  • 1 1/2 sticks (12 Tbsp) butter, room temp
  • 1 1/2 cups sugar
  • 3 large eggs
  • 2 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup milk
  • 3/4 cup sour cream
  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • 1/2 tsp sea or kosher salt
  • Cake Instructions
  • Pour into pan and bake:
  • Fresh Strawberry Frosting
  • For Sheet Pan:
  • 1 cup frozen strawberries, thawed
  • 3 sticks (1 1/2 cups) butter, room temp
  • 1/2 tsp sea or kosher salt
  • 6–7 cups powdered sugar
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • For 9x13:
  • 1/2 cup frozen strawberries, thawed
  • 2 sticks (1 cup) butter, room temp
  • 1/2 tsp sea or kosher salt
  • 3 1/2 cups powdered sugar
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • Frosting Instructions
  • Gradually add powdered sugar
  • Add vanilla, then slowly mix in strawberry purée:
  • Sheet pan: start with 1/2 cup, add more if needed
  • 9 x13: start with 1/4 cup, add more if needed

Steps

  1. Secret tip: use frozen strawberries for the most intense strawberry flavor (fresh can be watery and dull the taste).
  2. Makes a sheet pan (13x18) cake, but I included a 9x13 + layer cake version too.
  3. And the frosting is the real star. It’s my take on that classic strawberry sprinkle frosting we all grew up loving—except this version tastes real, fresh, and so much better.
  4. Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease your baking dish (sheet pan or 9x13).
  5. In a mixer or large bowl, beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
  6. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
  7. Mix in vanilla, milk, and sour cream. (It may look curdled—totally normal.)
  8. Gradually mix in flour, baking powder, and salt. Stir until just combined.
  9. Sheet pan: 18–25 minutes
  10. Bake until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out mostly clean and the edges begin to pull away from the pan. Let the cake cool completely before frosting.
  11. Blend thawed strawberries into a smooth purée.
  12. In a mixer or large bowl, beat butter and salt until fluffy.
  13. Beat until smooth, fluffy, and spreadable.
  14. Tip: If the frosting gets too soft, add a little more powdered sugar until it thickens back up.
  15. Frost the cooled cake, slice, and enjoy. This one won’t last long.

Sourdough Brown Bread

Sweet and delicious, this is the best sourdough brown bread recipe that tastes just like the Cheesecake Factory bread. Made with 100% sourdough, whole wheat and bread flour, you will love this copycat bread.

Serves 4Prep 20 minCook 30 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1 cup water
  • 1/2 cup sourdough starter
  • ¼ cup honey
  • 2 tablespoon molasses
  • 2 cup white bread flour
  • 1 ¾ cup whole wheat flour
  • 2 tablespoon cocoa powder
  • 1 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 3 tablespoon unsalted butter (melted)
  • oats for dusting top

Steps

  1. In a medium bowl, mix water, honey, molasses, melted butter and sourdough starter.
  2. Add in bread flour, whole wheat flour, salt, and cocoa powder. Mix until a smooth dough has formed.
  3. Transfer dough to a clean bowl, cover it and let it rise until it doubles. It will take from 8 to 10 hours. Remember to leave in a warm spot.
  4. After the first rise divide dough into 4 pieces. Using your hands or a rolling pin, open each piece in a rectangle. Roll into a cylinder and pinch to close. Roll the tops of the loaves in oats.
  5. Place in a lined baking sheet or in a mini loaf pan, cover and let rise for 2 more hours or until loaves almost double, and look puffy and light.
  6. Preheat oven to 350°F. Uncover loaves and bake them for 30 to 35 minutes.
  7. Let loaves cool for 15 minutes before slicing.

Source: The Farmstyle

Sourdough Chicken Pot Pie Recipe

Flaky sourdough crust packed full of creamy gravy, moist chicken and hearty veggies, your whole family will surely love this comforting Sourdough Chicken Pot Pie Recip.

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 30 minTotal 60 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • My Sourdough Pie Crust Recipe
  • 57 grams unsalted butter (4 Tablespoons )
  • 75 grams celery, 1/4 inch slices (1/2 cup, about 2 stalks )
  • 150 grams carrots, 1/4 inch slices (1 cup, about 2 large carrots )
  • 50 grams onion, diced (1/3 cup, about 1 small onion)
  • 2 cloves garlic (minced)
  • 350 grams chicken stock (1 1/2 cups )
  • 100 grams sourdough discard (1/3 cup )
  • 155 grams half and half (2/3 cup )
  • salt and pepper to taste
  • 450 grams cooked chicken, cubed (1 pound )
  • 75 grams frozen peas (1/2 cup )
  • 75 grams frozen corn (1/2 cup)
  • egg wash **

Steps

  1. Prepare my sourdough pie crust recipe through step 7 (this makes enough for a double-pie crust). Then, follow the instructions below. Long Ferment: Store the wrapped discs in the fridge for up to 3 days.
  2. In a large Dutch oven or pot, melt the butter, then add the celery, carrots and onions, saute over medium heat until they are tender.
  3. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute or until fragrant.
  4. Warm up the chicken stock in a liquid measuring cup. Add in the sourdough discard and whisk until incorporated. Slowly pour the broth mixture and half and half into the pot, stir, then bring to a simmer and cook until the mixture is a thick gravy consistency. Add the salt and pepper. Sometimes I like to add dried thyme as well.You can use active sourdough starter, just use the same amount in grams.
  5. Add the cooked, cubed chicken, frozen peas and frozen corn and stir until combined. Remove the filling from the heat and let it cool. If the filling is hot, it will melt the butter in the pie crust.
  6. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
  7. In the meantime, roll out the pie crust. Remove one of the pie dough discs out of the fridge and leave it at room temperature for about 10 minutes for easy rolling.
  8. On a lightly floured work surface, roll one of the discs into a 13-inch diameter circle. Carefully place it into a deep 9 inch pie dish that is at least 1.5 inches deep. Spoon the cool pie filling into the crust.
  9. Flour your work surface again and roll the second pie dough disc into a 10-inch diameter circle. Place this over the pie filling. Fold the excess dough behind the bottom crust, then crimp the crust with a fork or pinch with your clean fingers to seal. Cut 4 small slits with a sharp knife on the top pie crust to allow steam to escape.
  10. In a small bowl, whisk together an egg with milk. Using a pastry brush, brush the egg wash on the top crust.
  11. Bake at 425 degrees F for 30-35 minutes or until the top crust is gold brown. Check to see if the edges are browning too fast around 20 minutes. If necessary, cover them with a pie shield or cover with aluminum foil.
  12. Once baked, remove the pie from the oven and let it rest for 10-15 minutes before slicing and serving. Enjoy!

Source: Simplicity and a Starter

Sourdough Corn Dogs Recipe

Sourdough Corn Dogs are hand-dipped in a honey, sourdough batter and fried until crispy and golden brown.

Serves 12Prep 10 minCook 15 minTotal 25 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 12 hot dogs (choose your favorite)
  • 290 grams yellow cornmeal, fine (1 3/4 cups )
  • 175 grans all-purpose flour (1 1/4 cups )
  • 50 grams sugar (1/4 cup )
  • 14 grams baking powder (1 Tablespoon )
  • 1 gram salt (1/4 teaspoon )
  • 1 egg (beaten)
  • 360 grams milk (1 1/2 cups )
  • 140 grams sourdough discard (heaping 1/2 cup )
  • 14 grams unsalted butter, melted (1 Tablespoon )
  • 24 grams honey (1 Tablespoon )
  • neutral frying oil

Steps

  1. Pour neutral frying oil into a Dutch oven or a large pot, about 2 inches high. Heat to medium-high heat (350 F). I love using this frying thermometer to help keep the temperature consistent.Choose a neutral frying oil like vegetable, avocado or tallow.
  2. Remove the hot dogs from their packaging and pat dry with a paper towel. Insert a stick into each hot dog.
  3. In a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
  4. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg, milk, discard, melted butter, and honey until smooth.
  5. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Mix until all of the dry bites have been just incorporated, but be careful not to over mix! This can lead to a dense batter. It's okay if there are lumps, just like pancake batter.
  6. Pour the cornbread batter into a tall glass and dip one hot dog at a time. Allow any excess batter to dip off for 5 seconds, then place the top of the corn dog into the hot oil at an angle. Fry for 5-7 seconds before carefully dropping the entire sourdough corn dog into the oil, this prevents it from sticking to the bottom.
  7. Fry for 2-3 minutes, or until the Sourdough Corn Dogs are a deep golden brown. Use tongs or a spider wire ladle to turn the sourdough corn dogs in order for it to be fried on all sides.
  8. Remove the Sourdough Corn Dogs from the oil and place them on a wire rack.
  9. Serve hot with your favorite condiments. Enjoy!

Source: Simplicity and a Starter

Sourdough Corndogs

Sourdough Corndogs 🇺🇸 Who else loves getting corndogs at the fair?

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 20 minTotal 40 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 10 hot dogs
  • 2 c sourdough discard (I used unfed sourdough starter right out of the refrigerator.)
  • 1 c yellow cornmeal
  • 1/2 c milk (may need more or less depending on the hydration of your sourdough starter. )
  • 1/4 c sugar
  • 3 Tb honey
  • 1/2 tsp sea salt
  • 2 quarts Peanut oil or frying oil of your choice. (enough to fill your pan 2-3 inches deep. )
  • Cornstarch (For coating hot dogs )

Steps

  1. In a cask iron or heavy-duty frying pan heat your oil to 350 degrees Fahrenheit over medium heat.
  2. Prepare the hot dogs by patting them dry with a paper towel, skewering them on a stick, and rolling them in cornstarch. Make sure they are coated well, this will help the batter stick to the hot dog.
  3. Mix the cornmeal, salt, and sugar then add in the sourdough starter, and honey. Slowly pour in the milk a little at a time to watch for consistency. You want the batter to run off the wisk but thick enough to still form a peak off of the hot dog. If you get the batter to thin add a little flour to thicken.
  4. Fill a tall drinking glass or container with the batter. Dip the hot dogs into the batter to coat and carefully set them in the hot oil. Fry them until they are golden brown, roughly 30 seconds on each side. Remove them from the oil and let them sit on a paper towel for a few seconds to soak up any extra grease and serve immediately with your favorite dipping sauces.
  5. You can keep them in the refrigerator for up to a week and reheat them in the oven.
  6. To freeze make sure they cool off completely after frying and place in a ziplock bag, remove any access air. Freeze for up to 3 months and reheat them at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 20 minutes on a parchment-lined cookie sheet right out of the freezer. I would not recommend heating them in the microwave. The oven will keep them fresh and crispy, the microwave will make them go soggy.

Source: Life With Katie Donnelly · Original post

Sourdough Discard Crackers Recipe

Sourdough discard crackers are thin, crispy and have that amazing tang that you can only get with real sourdough! You'll never want to throw away your sourdough discard after your taste these addictive crunchy crackers!

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 60 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 3/4 cup discarded sourdough starter (stirred down)
  • 2 tablespoons butter (melted)
  • 1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 2 teaspoons dried herbs (Herbs de Provence)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt for sprinkling on top

Steps

  1. Preheat your oven to 325°F (162°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Melt the butter in a mixing bowl and let cool.
  2. Weigh the sourdough discard, dried herbs and salt into the bowl of melted butter and mix thoroughly until well combined. Use an off-set spatula to spread the mixture in a thin, even layer onto the parchment paper. Sprinkle the top with salt.
  3. Bake for 10 minutes. Remove from oven and score the crackers. Bake for an additional 20-50 minutes or until the crackers are golden brown. Let cool completely before breaking into squares. (Oven temperatures vary, check the crackers after 20 minutes into baking to make sure they do not over bake. See notes.)

Ingredients

  • 10 1/2 cups organic all purpose flour
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/3 cup olive oil or tallow
  • 1/2 cup warm water
  • 1 cup sourdough discard

Steps

  1. Add flour and salt to the bowl of a stand mixer and mix using the dough hook.

  8. Place the finished tortillas inside a tea towel and cover to keep soft.

Sourdough Pie Crust Recipe

Nothing says comfort food quite like a homemade pie. It's the perfect envelope for any pie-filling goodness! Flaky and flavorful, my grandma's knock-out pie crust recipe got a bit healthier with the added bonus of sourdough flavor.

Serves 16Prep 5 minTotal 65 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 240 grams all-purpose flour (1 3/4 cups)
  • 6 grams salt (1 teaspoon)
  • 3 grams baking powder (1/2 teaspoon)
  • 113 grams unsalted butter, frozen (1/2 cup)
  • 60 grams lard ** see substitutions below (1/3 cup)
  • 140 grams sourdough discard, cold (heaping 1/2 cup )
  • ice cold water (optional (1 teaspoon at a time))

Steps

  1. Before you begin this recipe, measure the lard in a measuring cup and place it in the freezer for at least 10 minutes to chill.
  2. Next, put flour, salt, and baking powder in the food processor.
  3. After 10 minutes, remove the lard from the freezer. Cut the frozen butter into cubes and place the butter and smaller pieces of lard in the food processor.
  4. Mix on dough or low setting until the mixture looks crumbly, about 15 seconds.
  5. Add the COLD discard to the food processor and mix again on dough until the dough forms.If the dough doesn't come together after mixing for at least 30 seconds, you may need to add ice-cold water. Continue adding teaspoon of ice water (one at a time) and mixing until the dough is formed.
  6. Remove the dough from the food processor and cut in half with a bench scraper or a sharp knife. Roll each section into two dough balls and flatten with your hands.
  7. Cover each piece with plastic wrap and pop them into the refrigerator to chill for at least one hour.You can store it in the fridge for up to 3 days to long-fermented the pie dough.
  8. Pull the dough out of the fridge and bring it to room temperature (about 15 minutes) for easy rolling.
  9. Unwrap the pie dough and place it on a lightly floured surface.
  10. With a floured rolling pin, roll from the center outward. Then turn the dough a quarter turn and repeat rolling.
  11. After rolling the dough full circle, add more flour to your work surface - you don't want the dough to stick!
  12. Flip the dough to the other side and roll it out until it is nice and thin, about 1/8 inch thick and a 12-inch circle.
  13. Using your rolling pin is the best way to maneuver your pie dough into a 9-inch pie dish! Roll the dough onto the rolling pin and unroll in the pie plate. Easy!

Source: Simplicity and a Starter

Southwest Stuffed Sweet Potatoes

Southwest Stuffed Sweet Potatoes made with ground turkey, black beans, corn, and cheese provide over 20 grams of protein and 9 grams of fiber per serving. A hearty, healthy dinner!

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 60 minTotal 75 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 6 medium sweet potatoes (8 ounces each, scrubbed clean)
  • 1 teaspoon avocado oil
  • 1 poblano pepper (seeded and diced)
  • 1 jalapeño pepper (seeded and diced)
  • ½ yellow onion (diced)
  • 1 pound 93% ground turkey
  • 3 cloves garlic (chopped)
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1 ½ teaspoons cumin
  • ½ cup black beans (rinsed and drained)
  • ½ cup frozen roasted corn
  • 1 tablespoon chopped cilantro (plus more for garnish)
  • 3/4 cup shredded pepper jack cheese
  • Greek yogurt (for serving)

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 400° F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Place the sweet potatoes on the prepared baking sheet and pierce each potato a few times with a fork. Transfer the sweet potatoes to the oven to roast for 45-60 minutes, until very tender and easily pierced with a knife. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly.
  3. In the meantime, prepare the filling. Heat the avocado oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the poblano, jalapeño, and onion to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables have softened slightly, 5-7 minutes.
  4. Add the turkey and garlic to the pan. Use a wooden spoon to break the turkey up into small pieces. Season with the salt and cumin and cook, stirring occasionally, until the turkey is cooked through, about 7 minutes.
  5. Add the black beans and corn, stir to combine and heat through. Remove from heat and add the cilantro, stir to incorporate.
  6. When the sweet potatoes are slightly cooled, cut them lengthwise and spread the potatoes open to make space for the filling. Use a measuring cup to stuff them and slightly compact the filling in. Top with cheese and broil until the cheese is melted and bubbly, 2-3 minutes.
  7. Top with greek yogurt and chopped cilantro.

Source: Skinnytaste

Southwest Style Dense Bean Salad

southwest style dense bean salad the full recipe is below!

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 15 minTotal 30 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1 lb chicken thighs
  • 1 tbsp avocado oil
  • 1 packet of taco seasoning
  • 1 can great northern beans, (rinsed and drained)
  • 1 can pinto beans, (rinsed and drained)
  • 1 red bell pepper, (diced)
  • 1 green bell pepper, (diced)
  • 2 jalapenos, (seeds removed and diced)
  • 1 cup roasted corn (or canned)
  • 1 handful of cilantro, (chopped)
  • 15 grape tomatoes, (halved)
  • 1 avocado, (added the day of)
  • ⅓ cup olive oil
  • 2 tbsp vinegar
  • Juice of ½ lime
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • ½ tsp onion powder
  • ½ tsp dried oregano
  • ½ tsp salt
  • ⅛ tsp pepper
  • ½ tsp paprika
  • 2 tsp cumin

Steps

  1. Add the chicken thighs, oil, and taco seasoning to a medium bowl. Toss until the chicken is fully coated on all sides, then set aside.
  2. Preheat a large pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the chicken and cook for 7-10 minutes, flipping halfway through, until fully cooked to an internal temp of 165°F. Remove from the pan and let rest while you prep the other ingredients.
  3. To make the vinaigrette, add all the vinaigrette ingredients to a bowl and whisk until smooth.
  4. Once the chicken has rested, cube it and add it to a large bowl. Add the beans, diced peppers, jalapeños, red onion, tomatoes, corn, cilantro, and southwest vinaigrette. Toss until everything is evenly combined.
  5. If eating right away, stir in the cubed avocado. If meal prepping, wait to add the avocado until the day you're serving. Enjoy!

Source: Cailee Eats · Original post

Spiced Chicken and Carrots

day two of sharing 10 days of high protein meals!!

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 30 minTotal 45 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 2 teaspoons kosher salt
  • 1 teaspoon ground black pepper
  • 2 teaspoons garlic powder
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 2 teaspoons smoked paprika
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil, (divided)
  • 1 pound carrots, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch slices
  • 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breast, pounded to 3/4-inch thick pieces
  • 1 lemon, halved
  • 1 cup low-fat or whole milk Greek yogurt (can substitute dairy-free yogurt)
  • 2 tablespoons finely chopped cilantro leaves, additional for garnishing
  • 1 teaspoon olive oil
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
  • 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1 cup jasmine rice, cooked for serving

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Prepare a large sheet pan.
  2. Make the spice mix: combine the salt, black pepper, garlic powder, oregano, and smoked paprika in a bowl, then evenly separate into two small bowls.
  3. In a large bowl, toss to coat the carrots in 1 tablespoon of the oil and one bowl (half) of the spice mix. Transfer to the sheet pan.
  4. Add the chicken to the same bowl with the remaining tablespoon of olive oil and the remaining spice mix. Toss to coat. Transfer to the sheet pan, spreading out the chicken and carrots so nothing is overlapping. Add the lemon halves, face down, on each end of the sheet pan. Bake until the carrots are lightly crisp on the outside and fork tender, and the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F, 25 to 30 minutes.
  5. While the chicken bakes, prepare the rice according to package instructions.
  6. Prepare the yogurt sauce: add the yogurt, cilantro, olive oil, black pepper, garlic powder, and salt to a bowl. Squeeze the roasted lemon halves into the bowl, then mix until evenly combined.
  7. To serve, plate even servings of the cooked rice and top with carrots and chicken. Add a dollop of the yogurt sauce on top and garnish with chopped cilantro.

  1. Prep the chicken: Cut the chicken into cubes. Add 1 Tbsp of the olive oil and the seasonings. Give it a toss until the chicken is coated. Set aside to let the chicken marinade at least 30 minutes while you make the other components of the bowl.
  2. Make the cilantro lime rice: cook rice according to the instructions on the package. Let it cool about 5-10 minutes and then add the cilantro, lime juice, olive oil, garlic powder, salt & black pepper. Mix to combine.
  3. Prep the Elote Dressing: while the rice is cooking, make the Elote dressing by mixing together the Greek yogurt, olive oil mayonnaise, lime zest, lime juice and spices.
  4. Make the Street Corn Salad: If using fresh ears of corn, cook it using your preferred cooking method and remove fresh corn kernels from the cob with a sharp knife. Remove the pulp and seeds from the jalapeno. Chop the jalapeno, red pepper, red onion, and cilantro. To assemble the salad, add the corn, bell pepper, jalapeno, cilantro, red onion and cotija cheese to a large bowl. Add half of the Elote dressing and mix.
  5. Cook the chicken: heat a large skillet on medium-high heat. Add olive oil and heat until it shimmers. Add the marinated chicken and cook for 3-4 minutes on one side, undisturbed. Flip and cook another 3-4 minutes until fully cooked to an internal temperature of 165℉ (75°C)
  6. Assemble the bowls: Add the romaine (optional), rice, chicken and street corn salad to a bowl. Top it with more dressing, a squeeze of lime, and your favorite toppings!
  7. Hint: meal prep in advance by making the corn salsa and dressing ahead of time!

The Best Chocolate Chip Cookies

Your search for the best chocolate chip cookies ends here. This chewy chocolate chip cookie recipe is made with browned butter and huge chunks of chocolate for the perfect, crunchy on the outside, gooey in the middle cookie of your dreams. Pair one of these bad boys with glass of cold milk for the best cookies and milk of your life?

Serves 15Prep 1 hr 20 minCook 11 minTotal 1 hr 31 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 3/4 cup (168g) unsalted butter*
  • 1 cup (212g) packed light brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg + 1 large egg yolk, at room temperature
  • 1 tablespoon pure vanilla extract
  • 1 3/4 cup (220g) all-purpose flour
  • 3/4 teaspoon baking soda
  • 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt + more flaky sea salt for sprinkling
  • 1 1/4 cups (210g) semisweet or bittersweet chocolate chips (or roughly chopped chocolate)

Steps

  1. Place the butter in a small saucepan and set over medium low heat. Low heat is key to an even, golden browning! Use a silicone spatula to stir and scrape the butter from the bottom and sides of the pan every 10 to 15 seconds. At first, the butter will melt and foam, then over time the foam bubbles will get smaller and the butter will begin to emit a warm, nutty aroma. Continue to cook the butter, occasionally stirring and scraping with your spatula, until the butter begins to take on color and you see small floating brown bits, about 5 to 7 minutes (these are the milk solids in your butter separating and toasting). Once the butter is golden brown, remove it from the heat and allow it to cool in the saucepan for about 5 minutes. You want it to cool down enough that it’s pretty warm, but not scalding hot to the touch.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the brown butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar. Use a silicone spatula to mix together. Add the egg, extra egg yolk, and vanilla and mix well.
  3. Add in the flour, baking soda, salt and fold until no streaks of flour remain, being careful not to overmix your batter. The dough should be soft but not sticky, so when you touch it with your finger, it gives just a little.
  4. Fold in the chocolate chips until evenly distributed. Do not over mix. Cover the bowl and place it in the fridge to chill for at least 1 hour (and up to overnight).
  5. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper. Remove the dough from the fridge and allow it to soften at room temperature until it’s scoopable (about 20 minutes). Use a 1 ½ ounce cookie scoop to portion out equal amounts of dough. Place on the prepared baking sheets, spacing the dough 2 inches apart.
  6. Bake until the cookies have puffed up and are light golden brown around the edges but still somewhat soft in the middle, 12 to 13 minutes. Remove the baking sheet from the oven, sprinkle with flaky sea salt (if using), and allow the cookies to cool slightly on the baking sheet before serving.

Source: Broma Bakery

Lactation Cookies

These soft, chewy lactation cookies are made with oats, flaxseed, brewer’s yeast and chocolate chips. They’re vegan, easy to make and freezer-friendly for a convenient breastfeeding snack.

Serves 24Prep 15 minCook 10 minTotal 25 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 2 Tablespoons ground flaxseed
  • ⅓ cup water
  • 2 ¼ cups quick cooking oats (certified gluten-free if needed)
  • ¾ cup oat flour (certified gluten-free if needed)
  • 3 Tablespoons brewer's yeast (labeled gluten-free if needed)
  • ½ teaspoon baking soda
  • ½ teaspoon baking powder
  • ½ teaspoon cinnamon
  • ¼ teaspoon sea salt
  • ½ cup melted coconut oil
  • 1 cup coconut sugar (brown sugar works as well )
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla
  • ½ cup chocolate chips (dairy-free, if needed)

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F and spray two baking sheets with cooking spray or line with parchment or Silpat and set aside.
  2. Make flax eggs by whisking together ground flaxseed with water. Set aside.
  3. In a medium bowl, mix together oats, oat flour, brewer's yeast, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon and salt. Set aside.
  4. In a large mixing bowl mix together oil, sugar, flaxseed eggs and vanilla until smooth.
  5. Add dry ingredients into the bowl with the wet ingredients and stir until just combined.
  6. Gently stir in chocolate chips.
  7. Using a spoon or cookie scoop, drop cookie dough by rounded tablespoonfuls about 2 inches apart on baking sheets. Press each cookie down with a fork a bit.
  8. Bake for 10 minutes, or until golden brown. The cookies may seem a little soft, but do not over bake or they’ll get too crisp. Remove from oven and let cool on sheet for about 5 minutes or until they start to harden up a bit. At this point you can transfer the cookies to a wire rack to cool completely.
  9. Store cookies in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 10 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

Toffee Cookie Bars

Serves 12Prep 20 minCook 35 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (227 g) unsalted butter, (melted)
  • 1 cup (220 g) light brown sugar (packed)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 2 eggs (room temperature)
  • 1 tsp (5 mL) vanilla extract
  • 2 cups (240 g) all purpose flour (spooned & leveled, not packed)
  • 1/2 tsp (2.5 g) baking soda
  • 1/4 tsp (1 g) baking powder
  • 1 tsp (3 g) Argo corn starch
  • 1/2 tsp (3 g) salt
  • 28 g (2 tbsp) unsalted butter
  • 73 g (⅓ cup) packed brown sugar
  • 60 g (2 tbsp + 2 tsp) light corn syrup
  • 21 mL (1 tbsp + 1 tsp) heavy whipping cream
  • 6 g (2 tsp) cornstarch
  • 10 mL (2 tsp) water
  • pinch flaky sea salt
  • 1.7 mL (⅓ tsp) vanilla extract
  • 4 oz Melted dark (or semi sweet) chocolate (for drizzling)
  • More flaky sea salt for topping

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F (177°C). Grease and 8×8 pan with butter and line with parchment paper (this helps with easy pan removal later). To make the cookie base, in a large bowl, using a rubber spatula, mix together butter, brown sugar and granulated sugar. Mix until smooth. Add the eggs and vanilla, mix again until incorporated.
  2. In a separate bowl, gently whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cornstarch. Slowly add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, mix as you go.
  3. Evenly spread dough into the prepared pan and bake for 33-34 minutes, or until the base is golden brown, the edges are set and there is a just a slight jiggle like jello in the middle. Note: ovens do vary so please look for visual cues rather than at the clock. The bars could need more or less time depending on the oven. Best rule of thumb is to start checking for visual cues around 28-30 minutes.
  4. When the cookie base is almost done (about 5 minutes left of baking), work on the toffee layer. Add water and cornstarch to a small bowl. Mix well with a fork until all cornstarch chunks disappear. Set to the side.
  5. In a saucepan, over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the brown sugar, heavy cream, salt and corn syrup. Whisk constantly until mix comes to a boil and pour in the cornstarch/water slurry. Stir until the mix thickens, about 1-2 minutes (please do not cook the mixture any longer than 1 - 2 minutes). Then mix in the vanilla. The mixture should still be runny (so that we can pour over the baked blondies).
  6. When the cookie base is done baking, pour the hot toffee over the base *Note: try to spread the toffee in and around the bars as much as possible. You can do this by moving the pan around and letting the toffee spill all over the bars. Our goal is not let too much of the toffee pool in the middle of the cookie base.
  7. Bake for another 10 minutes. Toffee should be bubbling. Remove from the oven, let the bars rest for about 2 hours. To melt the dark chocolate, simply place chocolate chips or chunks in a heat proof bowl, microwave in 10 second intervals, stir and repeat until chocolate is completely melted.
  8. When ready to serve, lift bars from the pan, drizzle with the melted chocolate and sea salt! Enjoy!

Pumpkin Bread

Kids love it, grown-ups love it...this pumpkin bread is hard to beat!

Serves 24Prep 20 minCook 65 minTotal 90 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour, (spooned into measuring cup and leveled-off)
  • ½ teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • ½ teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 3/4 cup (1½ sticks) unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 cups sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 (15-oz) can 100% pure pumpkin (I use Libby's)

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C )and set an oven rack in the middle position. Generously grease two 8 x 4-in (20 x 10-cm) loaf pans with butter and dust with flour (alternatively, use a baking spray with flour in it, such as Pam with Flour or Baker's Joy).
  2. In a medium bowl, combine the flour, salt, baking soda, baking powder, cloves, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Whisk until well combined; set aside.
  3. In a large bowl of an electric mixer, beat the butter and sugar on medium speed until just blended. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Continue beating until very light and fluffy, a few minutes. Beat in the pumpkin. The mixture might look grainy and curdled at this point—that's okay.
  4. Add the flour mixture and mix on low speed until combined.
  5. Turn the batter into the prepared pans, dividing evenly, and bake for 65 to 75 minutes, or until a cake tester inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the loaves cool in the pans for about 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely. Once completely cooled, cover the loaf with aluminum foil or store it in a cake keeper and keep it at room temperature for up to 3 days.

  • Olive oil

  • 1 tsp dried oregano
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 3/4 cup whole wheat orzo
  • 1 1/2 cups chicken broth, plus more as needed
  • 2 garlic cloves , minced
  • 2 cups chopped spinach
  • 8 oz feta cheese, divided
  • Zest of 1 lemon
  • Chopped cherry tomatoes
  • Chopped cucumber
  • Sliced pepperoncini
  • Chopped pickled red onions, plus a splash of the brine
  • Chopped fresh dill or parsley

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Cut the bell peppers into wide, flat pieces and arrange them in a single layer on a 10x15-inch jelly roll pan or similar rimmed baking sheet coated with cooking spray. If you like your peppers on the softer side, drizzle them with olive oil and bake for about 6 minutes while you make the filling. If you prefer a little more crunch, you can skip the pre-bake.
  2. Heat a drizzle of olive oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground turkey, Greek seasoning, oregano and garlic powder and cook, breaking up the turkey, until browned.
  3. Add the orzo and chicken broth. Cook, stirring frequently, until the orzo is almost tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed, adding an extra splash of broth as needed if the pan gets dry before the orzo is cooked through. Stir in the garlic and spinach and cook until the spinach is wilted. Turn off the heat and stir in half of the feta and all of the lemon zest. Taste and season with salt, pepper or additional Greek seasoning as needed.
  4. Spoon the turkey-orzo mixture over the pepper pieces. Crumble the remaining feta over the top and bake for about 12 minutes, until the peppers are crisp-tender and the feta is lightly browned.
  5. Meanwhile, make the Greeko de Gallo by tossing together the tomatoes, cucumber, pepperoncini, pickled onions, a splash of the pickled onion brine, a drizzle of olive oil and fresh dill or parsley.
  6. Pile the Greeko de Gallo over the hot stuffed peppers, finish with a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil and serve.

Ultimate Crumbl Peanut Butter Cookie Copycat

This ultimate Crumbl Peanut Butter Cookie Copycat recipe is a perfect knockoff of those huge cookies sold at your local Cumbl Bakery. With peanut butter in three different layers, these super soft & tender cookies are melt-in-your-mouth delicious!

Serves 14Prep 17 minCook 10 minTotal 60 min

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1 cup peanut butter chips
  • ¼ cup peanut butter (creamy)
  • 2 tbsp powdered sugar
  • 1 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1⅓ cup cake flour
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • 1 tbsp cornstarch
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1 cup butter (softened)
  • 1 cup granulated sugar (plus extra for rolling)
  • 1 cup light brown sugar (packed)
  • 1 cup peanut butter (creamy)
  • 2 tsp vanilla extract
  • 2 large eggs
  • 2-4 tbsp peanut butter (creamy)

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 410°F.
  2. Place peanut butter chips and peanut butter in a bowl. Microwave for 1 minute. Stir until fully combined. Stir in the powdered sugar.
  3. Using a 1 tablespoon scoop or a tablespoon measuring spoon, scoop the filling onto a cookie sheet that has been lined with wax paper or parchment. It should make 14 disks. Set in the freezer while you make the dough.
  4. Mix flours, powder, soda, cornstarch, and salt in a large bowl.
  5. In a separate bowl or stand mixer, beat together the softened butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar on medium speed until light and fluffy, 3 minutes. Add in peanut butter and mix until well combined. Add in vanilla and eggs, one at a time, scraping down the bowl after each addition.
  6. Add in dry ingredients on low speed until just incorporated and there are no dry pockets.
  7. Using a 3.25 ounce scoop (or ⅓ cup measuring cup plus one tablespoon of dough), fill it ⅔ of the way with dough. Add 1 frozen filling disc, then fill the rest of the scoop up with dough to cover the filling. Roll in sugar and place on a parchment lined cookie sheet. Since these are so large only 6 cookies will fit on each baking sheet. Use a flat measuring cup to lightly flatten the cookie dough. Set in the freezer for 30 minutes.
  8. Bake at 410° for 10 minutes. Allow to cool on the cookie sheet for 10 minutes. Then use a spatula to carefully transfer them to a cooling rack.
  9. Once cookies are cool, microwave peanut butter until loose. Drizzle with a spoon in a random pattern. For a more exacting look, place melted peanut butter in a zip bag and cut a small hole in the end and drizzle.

Viral Chuck Roast

VIRAL CHUCK ROAST✨ my most popular recipe for good reason!

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1 boneless beef chuck roast (about 4 pounds)
  • 2 teaspoons kosher sea salt
  • 1 teaspoon black pepper

Steps

  1. Preheat your oven to 325. Season the roast generously on both sides with salt and pepper. Add to a baking large casserole dish or Dutch oven, cover (with a lid or foil), and bake for 1 hr per pound of meat.
  2. Remove the roast from the oven and raise the oven temperate to 425.
  3. Using two forks, shred the meat into large chunks. (If the roast is not pulling apart easily, put it back in the oven for 30 min).
  4. Toss the shredded pieces of roast around in the rendered fat and place it back in the oven, uncovered, for 20-25 minutes until you see some nice crispy ends.
  5. Serve with mashed potatoes or roasted vegetables and enjoy!
  6. FAQs:
  7. My roast is more/less than 4 lbs, how long should I cook it?
  8. Use the “hour per pound” method but I’ve found a minimum of 2.5 hour is needed even for smaller roasts. So if your roast is 2 pounds = 2.5 hours; 6 pounds = 6 hours.
  9. How do I choose a good beef chuck roast?
  10. Look for nice fatty roast with lots of marbling. A roast that is too lean will not render enough juice. (Note: I have hit or miss luck with grass-fed roasts. Most are just too tough/lean and don’t render enough fat for this preparation.)
  11. How many people does this serve?
  12. A 4-pound roast serves 6-7 people.
  13. Do I need to sear it first?
  14. Nope! The last part of the cook will give it some nice crispy bits without searing.
  15. Did you add liquid?
  16. No, that is the juice rendered from the meat.
  17. .
  18. .

  • 1 tsp onion powder
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp pepper
  • 1 tbsp avocado oil
  • Juice of 1/2 lime
  • Fresh Cilantro
  • Cheddar cheese
  • Sliced avocados
  • Sour cream

Steps

  1. I prefer to pre-bake my chicken in the oven while I'm preparing everything else. To make the chicken, simply season with salt and pepper and place it in the oven at 400 for 20-25 minutes until fully cooked. Once cooked, shred it and set it aside for later.
  2. In a large pot, add 1 tbsp avocado oil to medium heat.
  3. Add in the onions and jalapenos and saute for 2-3 minutes until soft. Add the minced garlic and saute for another minute until fragrant.
  4. Add all the seasoning into the pot and mix until the onions and jalapenos are well coated. Saute for one more minute.
  5. Next, add the beans, corn, green chilis, and chicken stock, mix well, and bring to a boil.
  6. Cover with a lid and reduce the temperature to low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes to let the flavors come together!

  8. Finally, add the shredded cooked chicken, heavy cream, and the juice of half a lime. Give it one more good mix.

Ingredients

  • 12 oven-ready lasagna noodles
  • 1 lb ground chicken
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • 3 cups fresh spinach, (roughly chopped)
  • 2 1/2 cups shredded mozzarella, (divided)
  • 1/2 cup grated parmesan
  • 2-3 tbsp pesto (used on top at the very end)
  • Fresh basil for topping (optional
  • 3 tbsp butter
  • 5 cloves garlic, (minced)
  • 3 tbsp flour
  • 3 cups milk
  • 1/3 cup basil pesto
  • 3/4 tsp salt
  • 1/4 tsp black pepper
  • 1 1/4 cups ricotta
  • 1/3 cup grated parmesan
  • 1 egg
  • 1/2 tsp salt

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 400℉.
  2. Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the olive oil and once hot, add the ground chicken. Cook for 5-7 minutes, occasionally breaking up the meat, until almost fully cooked.
  3. Season with salt and pepper, then add the chopped spinach. Sauté for a few minutes until the spinach has wilted. Remove the meat mixture from the skillet and set aside in a bowl.
  4. In the same skillet, melt the butter over medium heat. Once melted, whisk in the flour until it forms a paste, about 1 minute. Slowly pour in the milk, whisking continuously until fully incorporated.
  5. Let the sauce simmer for 3-4 minutes, until slightly thickened. Remove from the heat and stir in the salt, pepper, and pesto. Set aside until ready to assemble.
  6. In a small bowl, prepare the ricotta layer by mixing together the ricotta, parmesan, egg, and salt until well combined.
  7. Grease a 9×13-inch baking dish and begin assembling the lasagna.
  8. Spread about ¾ cup of the sauce on the bottom of the pan. Add 3–4 lasagna noodles, followed by half of the ricotta mixture, half of the chicken mixture, ½ cup mozzarella cheese, and 1 cup of sauce.
  9. Repeat the layers once more using the remaining ricotta and chicken.
  10. Finish with a final layer of noodles and the remaining sauce. Top with the remaining mozzarella and parmesan cheese. If desired, add a few small dollops of extra pesto on top.
  11. Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
  12. Remove the foil and bake for another 10 minutes, until bubbly and lightly golden.
  13. Let the lasagna rest for 10 minutes before cutting and serving.
  14. Finish with fresh basil on top, if desired.

Ingredients

  • 3 large zucchini
  • 1 lb ground beef
  • 1, 16oz jar marinara sauce
  • 1 cup ricotta cheese
  • 1/2 cup grated parmesan cheese
  • 1 small onion, (chopped)
  • 3 tbsp italian seasoning, (divided)
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1 tsp pepper
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 tbsp avocado oil
  • 1 tbsp fresh basil, (chopped)

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 400℉.
  2. Add 1 tbsp of avocado oil to a large skillet on medium-high heat. Once heated, add the ground turkey and cook for 5-7 minutes until brown.
  3. Once browned, add in the chopped onion and saute a few minutes until soft.
  4. Once done, add the entire jar of sauce, 1 tbsp of Italian seasoning, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp pepper. Mix well, cover with a lid, and bring the temperature down to low. Let it simmer until it's time to put it in the baking dish.
  5. Meanwhile, cut your zucchini in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds, leaving a hollow center. Make sure not to scrape it too thin! Then, lay them down at the bottom of a baking dish.
  6. Next, make the ricotta filling. Add ricotta cheese, parmesan cheese, and 2 tbsp of Italian seasoning to a bowl, then mix.
  7. Add about 1/2 of the ricotta cheese filling to the base of each zucchini, leaving about 1/2 cup of the filling to add to the top.
  8. Add the meat mixture to each piece of zucchini. I really like to pile it on here!
  9. Top it with dollops of the rest of the ricotta mixture and a sprinkle of parmesan cheese.
  10. Cover with foil, and bake for 30 minutes.
  11. After 30 minutes, pull off the foil and place it back in the oven for about 10 minutes, uncovered until the cheese is melted and starts to become golden. Top with freshly chopped basil. Serve immediately and enjoy!

Source: Cailee Eats · Original post

  • salt and black pepper
  • chili flakes
  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • 1 1/2 cups grated parmesan cheese

Steps

  1. 1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta according to package directions until al dente. Remove 1/2 cup pasta cooking water. Drain.2. Meanwhile, melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the lemon slices. Sear until the lemon is caramelized, about 1 minute per side. Remove the lemon from the skillet. Finely chop the lemon slices and mix with the basil.3. To the same skillet, add 4 tablespoons butter and the onion. Cook until caramelized, 8-10 minutes. Stir in the garlic, zucchini, thyme, and season with salt, pepper, and chili flakes. Cook another 5 minutes until golden. 4. Add 1/2 cup pasta cooking water and the cream, stirring until smooth. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened. Stir in the parmesan, then toss in the pasta. Cook for 2 minutes. Remove from the heat. 5. Serve topped with the reserved lemon/basil mix. Twirl the pasta up with the sauce and zucchini. EAT and ENJOY!

  • mozzarella
  • marinara sauce
  • white wine
  • rigatoni
  • pasta water

Steps

  1. Brown the ground beef in a pan with olive oil.
  2. Add garlic, half of a red bell pepper, and onions to the beef.
  3. Season with garlic powder, oregano, thyme, rosemary, pepper, and salt.
  4. In a bowl, mix 15 ounces of ricotta, one egg, garlic powder, thyme, a pinch of salt, and half a cup of grated Parmesan cheese.
  5. Stir in one cup of freshly shredded mozzarella and lots of pepper into the ricotta mixture.
  6. Add the cooked beef to the sauce and mix in a whole jar of marinara and a little bit of white wine.
  7. Combine two to three scoops of the sauce with the ricotta mixture and mix well.
  8. Dump the cooked rigatoni pasta into the mixture and mix everything together.
  9. Add some sauce to the bottom of a baking dish, then layer in the pasta mixture, mozzarella, and Parmesan cheese.
  10. Repeat layering with more sauce, fresh mozzarella, and Parmesan cheese until all ingredients are used, finishing with sauce and cheese on top.
  11. Bake at 350°F for about 15 minutes, then broil for an additional two minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

  • 2 small tortillas
  • Blend cheese (for topping)

Steps

  1. Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces.
  2. Coat the chicken with olive oil.
  3. Mix flour, baking powder, garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper in a mug.
  4. Coat the chicken in the seasoning mixture, ensuring it's not too floury.
  5. Place foil in the air fryer and add the coated chicken.
  6. Cook the chicken in the air fryer at 375°F for 13 minutes, flipping halfway through.
  7. While the chicken is cooking, prepare the coleslaw by mixing raw coleslaw mix with mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, salt, pepper, and dill to your desired consistency.
  8. Set up a sauce station with buffalo sauce and ranch, using more buffalo sauce than ranch.
  9. Warm two small tortillas in the microwave until soft.
  10. Check the chicken to ensure it is cooked through.
  11. Dump the cooked chicken into the sauce bowl and mix to coat evenly.
  12. Assemble the tacos by adding blended cheese and a generous amount of coleslaw on top.

  • 2 cups half and half

  • black pepper
  • red pepper flakes
  • 1 package Pillsbury Grands biscuits
  • 6 eggs
  • splash of milk
  • 1 1/2 cups cheese
  • gravy

Steps

  1. Brown breakfast sausage in a pan.
  2. Remove half of the cooked sausage from the pan and set it aside.
  3. Stir in butter into the pan with the remaining sausage.
  4. Stir in flour and let it cook down for at least 3 minutes.
  5. Slowly stir in half and half, about 1/2 a cup at a time.
  6. Season the mixture with slap your mama, black pepper, and red pepper flakes until it thickens, then set aside.
  7. Cut each biscuit from a package of Pillsbury Grands into nine pieces.
  8. In a mixing bowl, crack eggs, add a splash of milk and slap your mama, and mix well.
  9. Put the biscuit pieces in a greased 9 by 13 baking dish.
  10. Sprinkle the reserved sausage over the biscuits.
  11. Top with cheese.
  12. Spread the egg mixture over the cheese and biscuits.
  13. Top with gravy and then add one more cup of cheese on top.
  14. Bake in the oven at 350°F for about 35 to 40 minutes.

  • 1 tbsp maple syrup

Steps

  1. Instructions:
  2. Boil dates and soak in the warm water for about 10 minutes to soften them. Drain and set aside.
  3. In a blender or food processor, combine the cottage cheese, milk, soaked dates, vanilla extract (if using), maple syrup, and salt (if using). Blend until smooth and creamy.
  4. Pour the chia seeds into a bowl with the blended mixture and stir. Mix well to ensure the seeds are evenly distributed.
  5. Cover the bowl or jar and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight. The chia seeds will absorb the liquid and create a pudding-like texture.

  • 2 cups sharp cheddar cheese, freshly shredded shredded, plus extra for topping
  • 1 cup Colby Jack cheese, freshly shredded

Steps

  1. In a large skillet over medium heat, cook ground beef with ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp black pepper, and ½ tsp garlic powder until browned. Remove from skillet and set aside.
  2. In the same skillet, melt butter. Add onion, grated carrot, and garlic. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
  3. Stir in chopped broccoli florets and cook for 4–5 minutes, until slightly tender.
  4. Return beef to skillet. Pour in milk and heavy whipping cream. Simmer for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
  5. Stir in Dijon mustard, ½ tsp salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp smoked paprika, and ¼ tsp black pepper.
  6. Reduce heat to low. Add cheddar and Colby Jack in small handfuls, stirring after each addition until completely melted and smooth.
  7. Spoon the cheesy broccoli beef mixture over bowls of hot cooked rice or pasta, garnish with extra cheddar cheese, and serve immediately.

  3. Remove from the heat and season with the salt, pepper, and sage and mix well. Carefully pour off any excess oil and set aside to cool.
  4. Whisk the eggs in a bowl. Add the pork mixture and 1 cup of the cheese and mix well. Add the almond flour, coconut flour, and baking powder and mix until just combined.
  5. Scoop about 12 balls of dough onto the baking sheet, spacing them 1 to 2 inches apart. Lightly coat your palms with oil and press gently down on top of each ball to form a biscuit. Evenly sprinkle each with the remaining 1/2 cup cheddar and bake for 12 to 14 mins, until the cheese is melted and the biscuits are baked through and lightly browned.

  3. Mash five overripe bananas in a separate bowl.
  4. Add two eggs, one teaspoon of vanilla extract, half a cup of brown sugar, one stick of melted butter, and half a cup of sourdough discard to the mashed bananas.
  5. Use a hand mixer to mix the wet ingredients for about 20 seconds.
  6. Pour the wet ingredients into the bowl of dry ingredients and mix until well incorporated using a spatula or large spoon.
  7. Fold in eight ounces of semi-sweet chocolate chips gently.
  8. Spray the inside of a 9 by 5 loaf pan with cooking spray and pour the batter into the pan.
  9. Bake in a preheated oven at 350 degrees for about 50 minutes to one hour, keeping an eye on it towards the end until it is golden brown.

Creamy Chicken Orzo

Serves 4

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1 Tbsp Olive Oil
  • 1 lb Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts, cut into bite-size pieces
  • 10 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt, divided
  • 1/2 tsp Black Pepper
  • 2 Tbsp Butter, divided
  • 1 Small Yellow Onion, diced small
  • 3 Garlic Cloves , finely chopped
  • 1 Cup Orzo
  • 5 3/4 Cups Whole Milk, divided
  • 1/2 Cup Chicken Stock
  • 10 oz Broccoli Crowns, chopped small (4 Cups)
  • 1 Tbsp Lemon Juice
  • Freshly Grated Parmesan Cheese, for serving
  • Chopped Fresh Parsley, for serving

Steps

  1. In a large skillet over medium heat, heat the olive oil until shimmering. Add the chicken and season with 1 tsp of the salt and all the pepper. Spread the chicken into one layer and let cook undisturbed for 2-3 mins until golden brown, then continue cooking while stirring for 2-3 more mins until cooked through. Transfer into a bowl and set aside.
  2. In the same pan, melt 1 Tbsp of the butter, then add the onion and cook, stirring, until softened (3-5 mins). Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
  3. Stir in the orzo and toast for 1 min, then add 2+1/2 cups of the whole milk, the chicken stock, and remaining 1+1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often to prevent sticking.
  4. Cook uncovered for 8-10 mins, stirring often, until the orzo is al dente and the liquid has thickened into a creamy sauce. Stir in the chopped broccoli, and cook 4-6 more mins.
  5. Once the broccoli is tender and the orzo is creamy, stir the cooked chicken back into the pan and let it warm through for 1-2 mins.
  6. Stir in the remaining 1 Tbsp of butter and 1/4 cup of milk. Turn off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.
  7. Serve hot, topped with freshly grated parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley. Enjoy!

Creamy Coconut Peanut Noodles

Serves 4

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • PEANUT CURRY SAUCE
  • 3 tbsp natural peanut butter (smooth or crunchy)
  • 1 1/2 tbsp red curry paste (see note 1 for substitutions and about gluten)
  • 2 1/2 tbsp tamari (or all-purpose soy sauce, but this is not gluten-free)
  • 1 1/2 tbsp rice vinegar
  • 1 tbsp honey
  • 250 ml (1 cup) coconut milk
  • 1/2 tsp sesame oil
  • STIR-FRY
  • 250 g (9 oz) flat rice noodles
  • 2 tbsp neutral oil of choice (I used light olive oil)
  • 500 g (1 lb) minced (ground) chicken (see note 2 for substitutions)
  • 2 spring onions (scallions), thinly sliced, white and green parts separated, plus extra to garnish
  • 1 tsp freshly minced garlic
  • 1 tsp freshly minced ginger
  • 2 cups (150 g) finely shredded green cabbage
  • 1 cup (90 g) bean sprouts
  • 1 cup (250 ml) chicken stock
  • 1/4 cup (40 g) crushed roasted peanuts, to serve (optional)
  • Asian chilli oil or chilli crisp, to serve (optional)
  • Lime wedges

Steps

  1. – Combine the ingredients together in a small jug or bowl and whisk well to combine. Set aside.
  2. – Bring a large pot of water to the boil and cook the rice noodles until they are just pliable (between 2–3 minutes – they will continue cooking in the stir-fry). Drain, rinse under cold water to stop them cooking, then toss with 1 tablespoon of the oil to stop them sticking. Set aside.
  3. – Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in a large, deep, heavy-based pan or wok over medium–high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through.
  4. – Add the white parts of the spring onion along with the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute. Add the shredded cabbage and cook for 2–3 minutes until softened slightly.
  5. – Pour the peanut curry sauce into the pan with the chicken and cabbage. Stir to combine, then simmer for 1–2 minutes or until slightly thickened. Add the cooked noodles, bean sprouts and green parts of the spring onion, tossing with tongs to coat everything in the sauce. Add the chicken stock gradually (¼ cup/60 ml at a time) to loosen the sauce as needed (you may not need to use all the chicken stock depending on how thick you would like your sauce – the more chicken stock you add, the creamier and silkier the sauce will be).
  6. – Divide among bowls and top with extra spring onion, crushed roasted peanuts and a drizzle of Asian chilli oil or chilli crisp (if using). Serve with lime wedges.

Ingredients

  • GREEN CHILE
  • for recipe sent to DMs —or grab recipe below
  • Chicken filling:
  • 1 tablespoon oil

  • 1 medium-sized yellow onion, chopped
  • 2 garlic cloves , minced
  • 1 cup chicken broth
  • 1 (4 oz) can diced green chiles
  • 2 tablespoons adobo sauce
  • 1/4 cup diced green onion
  • 8 oz softened cream cheese
  • 2 cups corn
  • 2 tablespoons lime juice
  • Cornbread:
  • 1 cup cornmeal
  • 3/4 cup flour
  • 2 teaspoon baking powder
  • Dash of salt
  • 1 cup buttermilk
  • 1 large egg
  • 1/4 cup melted butter
  • 4 oz can diced green chiles
  • 1/4 cup diced green onions
  • 1/2 cup shredded cheese (pepper jack, cheddar)
  • 1 jalapeño sliced, for garnish

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 400°F.
  2. Lightly coat the chicken breasts with oil, then rub with taco seasoning. Heat an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat, drizzle with oil, and sear the chicken for 3–4 minutes per side. Add the onion and garlic and sauté for 1–2 minutes.
  3. Add the broth, green chiles, & adobo sauce to the skillet. Cover & simmer for 8–10 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F. Remove the chicken from the skillet & set aside to cool before shredding.
  4. Meanwhile, make the cornbread. In a bowl, whisk together the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, & salt. Add the buttermilk, egg, melted butter, green chiles, and green onions. Mix until just combined, then fold in the shredded cheese. Set aside.
  5. Once the chicken has been removed, add the cream cheese and corn to the skillet with the broth. Stir until the cream cheese has melted into the broth. Add the shredded chicken, lime juice, and green onions, stirring to combine. Spread the cornbread batter evenly over the top, almost completely covering the skillet. Top with sliced jalapeños and additional cheese, if desired.
  6. Bake for 30 minutes, or until the cornbread is golden brown and cooked through. Serve with a sour cream, avocado, & fresh cilantro.

Easy No Bake Homemade Protein Bars — Jazz Leaf

Serves 8

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • Protein Base:
  • 1 cup peanut butter or any nut butter
  • 2/3 cup protein powder
  • 1/4 cup agave
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • Chocolate Coating:
  • 2 oz chocolate bar (dark or semi-sweet)
  • 1/2 teaspoon coconut oil

Steps

  1. To create the protein base, in a large mixing bowl, combine the nut butter, protein powder, agave, vanilla and salt. Stir it together until a thick, dough-like consistency is formed. If the mixture is too dry, you can add a bit more nut butter or a splash of water to achieve the desired texture.
  2. Line a loaf pan with parchment paper. Press the protein mixture evenly into the bottom of the pan to form a solid base.
  3. To melt the chocolate, chop the chocolate bar into smaller pieces and add it into a microwave-safe bowl. Add the coconut oil to the chocolate. Microwave the chocolate in 30-second increments, stirring well after each interval, until the chocolate is completely melted and smooth.
  4. Pour the smooth melted chocolate on top of the protein base, and spread it evenly to coat the entire surface.
  5. Place the loaf pan into the freezer to chill and set for 60 minutes until the bars are firm.
  6. Once set, remove from the loaf pan and place it onto a cutting board, slice into 8 equal slices.
  7. Store the protein bars in an airtight container in the fridge for freezer! The fridge will yield a softer texture and the freezer will yield a more firm texture

French Onion Chicken Meatballs & Cheesy Orzo

Serves 4

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
  • 4 medium sweet Vidalia onions, chopped (about 6 cups)
  • 2 teaspoons kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
  • 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
  • 4 cloves garlic, grated or finely chopped
  • 3 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, divided
  • 4/3 cups freshly grated Gruyère cheese, divided
  • 1 large egg, whisked
  • 1/2 cup panko breadcrumbs
  • 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, plus more for garnish
  • 1 pound ground chicken
  • 1 1/2 cups dried orzo
  • 3 1/4 cups chicken stock
  • 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves
  • Nonstick cooking spray

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.
  2. Caramelize the onions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions to the pan and season with ½ teaspoon of the salt. Stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions are very soft and deeply caramelized, 35 to 40 minutes.
  3. Make a well in the center of the onions and add in the balsamic vinegar and garlic. Stir gently until the garlic becomes fragrant, about 30 seconds, then mix together with the onions until well combined. Continue to cook for another 2 to 3 minutes to let the flavors meld.
  4. Transfer ⅓ cup of the onions to a large mixing bowl and set aside cool slightly. Remove the skillet with the remaining onions from the heat.
  5. Make the meatballs: To the large bowl with the reserved onions, add 2 tablespoons of the parsley, ⅓ cup of the grated Gruyère, egg, panko, Dijon, 1 teaspoon of the salt, and ¼ teaspoon of the pepper and mix well. Add in the ground chicken and use your hands to mix until well combined. Use a 2-tablespoon cookie scoop or tablespoon measure to portion the mixture into balls (about 18–20 meatballs) and place them onto the prepared baking sheet. Use your hands to roll each meatball until smooth, and spray the tops lightly with nonstick cooking spray.
  6. Transfer the meatballs to the oven to bake until cooked through, 10 to 12 minutes. Then turn the broiler on high and cook until golden brown on top, about 2 minutes. Keep an eye on them as everyone’s broilers vary!
  7. Cook the Orzo: Meanwhile, return the skillet with the remaining onions back up to medium-high. Once sizzling, add the orzo and stir to combine. Add the chicken stock, thyme, ½ teaspoon of the salt, and ¼ teaspoon of the pepper. Raise the heat to high and bring the mixture to a boil, scraping any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Once boiling, reduce the heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is al dente and most of the liquid has been absorbed, about 10 minutes.
  8. Stir in the remaining 1 cup of Gruyère until melted and creamy. Remove from heat and taste to adjust for seasoning if desired.
  9. Nestle the cooked meatballs into the orzo mixture. Garnish with the remaining chopped parsley and a few cracks of black pepper. Serve family style straight out of the skillet, or divide evenly among serving bowls.

Ingredients

  • skillet:
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 2 large yellow onions, thinly sliced
  • 4 head garlic cloves, peeled and minced
  • 2 tbsp finely chopped thyme leaves (or 2 tsp dried thyme)
  • 1 tsp kosher salt
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper
  • 1 cup jasmine rice, rinsed
  • 3 cups low-sodium beef broth
  • 2 tbsp coconut aminos (sub tamari or reduced-sodium soy sauce)
  • 3/4 cup shredded gruyere or mozzarella cheese
  • chopped parsley leaves, for garnish
  • meatballs:
  • 1 pound 90% lean ground beef
  • 1 tbsp coconut aminos (sub tamari or low-sodium soy sauce)
  • 1 tsp kosher salt (omit if using tamari)
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 tsp onion powder
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 400F. Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
  2. Heat the olive oil in a large, deep, lidded skillet over medium heat. Once the oil is heated and shimmering, add the sliced onions. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions are very soft and caramelizing, 15 to 18 minutes (Note: if the onions start getting too browned, reduce heat to medium low until done caramelizing and add another tablespoon of oil.)
  3. While the onions caramelize, combine the ground beef, coconut aminos, garlic powder, and black pepper in a large bowl. Form about 18 two-tablespoon meatballs with lightly oil clean hands and place on the sheet pan, evenly spaced. Bake until at an internal temperature of 160F, 11 to 13 minutes.
  4. Add the garlic, thyme, salt, and black pepper to the skillet and continue cooking over medium heat until aromatic, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the rice and toast, stirring frequently, until golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the broth, coconut aminos, and 1/2 cup of water and stir to combine. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium low, cover, and cook until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy, 16 to 19 minutes, stirring halfway through to prevent sticking. If needed, add an additional 1/2 cup of water if it needs more when you stir halfway through.
  5. Reduce the heat to low, remove the lid, and place the meatballs on top of the rice. Sprinkle the mozzarella on top and cover to melt the cheese, 1 to 2 minutes (or transfer the skillet uncovered to the oven and broil on high for 1 to 2 minutes) . Remove the skillet from the heat, top with chopped parsley, and serve.

French Onion Pot Roast With Maple Garlic Mashed Potatoes

Dad

Ingredients

  • French Onion Pot Roast—
  • 3–4 lb chuck roast from @s1 foods
  • 2 tbsp olive oil @getgraza
  • 6 small yellow onions, thinly sliced
  • 2 tbsp butter
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/2 cup dry red wine
  • 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
  • 2 cups @kettleandfire beef broth
  • 1 tbsp dried thyme
  • 2 bay leaves
  • Maple Garlic Mashed Potatoes—
  • 3 lbs Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and chopped
  • 4 tbsp butter
  • 1/2 cup @organicvalley heavy cream
  • 1/4 cup sour cream
  • 3–4 cloves roasted or minced garlic
  • 1–2 tbsp pure maple syrup
  • Salt pepper, to taste
  • For the Top—
  • 1/2 cup shredded Gruyère cheese
  • 1/4 cup freshly grated Parmesan
  • Fresh thyme

Steps

  1. Sear the roast.
  2. Preheat oven to 325°F. Season the chuck roast generously with Kinder’s Sunday Pot Roast Seasoning.
  3. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the roast on all sides until browned. Remove and set aside.
  4. Caramelize the onions.
  5. Add butter and sliced onions to the same Dutch oven.
  6. Cook over medium-low heat for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onions are soft, golden and caramelized.
  7. Build the sauce.
  8. Add tomato paste and garlic. Cook for about 1 minute.
  9. Pour in the red wine and Worcestershire sauce. Stir and scrape up all the browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
  10. Let simmer for a few minutes until slightly reduced.
  11. Slow cook the roast.
  12. Pour in the beef broth and return the chuck roast to the Dutch oven.
  13. Cover and bake at 325°F for about 4 hours, or until the meat easily falls apart with a fork.
  14. Make the maple garlic mashed potatoes.:
  15. Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender. Drain well.
  16. Add potatoes, butter, sour cream, cream, garlic and maple syrup to a stand mixer. Mix until creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
  17. Shred + assemble.
  18. Remove the Dutch oven from the oven and shred the roast directly into the French onion gravy.

Ginger Chuck Roast

Serves 8

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 4 lbs chuck roast
  • Salt & pepper
  • 1 tbsp coconut sugar
  • 2 tbsp avocado oil
  • 1 yellow onion, halved and sliced thin
  • 1 tbsp ginger, minced
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 cups beef broth
  • 1/2 cup coconut aminos
  • 1 tbsp rice vinegar
  • 2 tbsp arrowroot starch
  • 2 tbsp green onion, sliced

Steps

  1. Oven Method:
  2. Set the roast on the counter for 30 minutes before preparing. Preheat the oven to 300 F.
  3. Trim some of the excess fat from the roast and slice into large chunks. Season well on all sides with salt and pepper and coconut sugar.
  4. Using a large dutch oven, heat the avocado oil over medium heat. Once the oil is shimmering, add the chuck roast. Sear on all sides to lightly brown. Set aside.
  5. Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the sliced onion. Lightly season with salt and pepper, sauteing for 3-4 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and saute for another 2 minutes, or until fragrant/
  6. Add the chuck roast back to the pot along with the broth, coconut aminos and rice vinegar. Place the lid on the pot and transfer to the oven.
  7. Allow to cook in the oven for 3.5 - 4 hours, or until the meat easily shreds. Start to check the meat at around 2.5-3 hours! Remove from the oven once cooked.
  8. Whisk 2 tbsp of arrowroot starch with about 3 tbsp of water (or beef broth) and add it to the pot roast, stirring it into the liquid to thicken.
  9. Allow to rest for 10-15 minutes before serving with a side of your choice like rice and vegetables.
  10. For the slow cooker method:
  11. Follow steps 2-4 above.
  12. Add the vegetables and roast to the slow cooker along with the broth, coconut aminos and rice vinegar. Cook on low for 6-8 hours, or until the roast easily shreds.
  13. Whisk 2 tbsp of arrowroot starch with about 3 tbsp of water (or beef broth) and add it to the pot roast, stirring it into the liquid to thicken.
  14. Allow to rest for 10-15 minutes before serving with a side of your choice like rice and vegetables.

  • 2 tbsp desiccated coconut

  • Pinch sea salt (optional)
  • Sprinkles (optional)

Steps

  1. Preheat the oven to 150°C fan-forced and line a 12-hole mini muffin tray with mini paper cases. You can also use regular muffin trays or a lined baking tray.
  2. In a small saucepan, gently melt the butter and honey until just combined. Do not allow the mixture to boil.
  3. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla extract and salt, if using.
  4. Place the cornflakes and desiccated coconut in a large bowl.
  5. Pour the honey mixture over the cornflakes and gently fold until evenly coated.
  6. Spoon the mixture into the mini cases and lightly press down.
  7. Bake for 8 minutes, or until lightly golden.
  8. Allow to cool completely in the tray to crisp up before serving.
  9. Don't skip the cooling step — the honey joys firm up and develop their signature crunch as they cool in the tray. Resist the urge to eat them warm!

Homemade Cookie Butter Coffee Syrup Recipe

Serves 2

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • Cookie Butter Coffee Syrup
  • 1 tbsp salted butter, browned
  • 1 cup water
  • 1/3 cup coconut sugar
  • 1/3 cup allulose
  • 3 cinnamon sticks
  • 1/8 tsp ginger
  • Tiny pinch nutmeg
  • Tiny pinch cloves
  • 1/2 tsp molasses
  • 1 1/2 tsp vanilla bean paste
  • 1/4 tsp butter extract
  • How I use it
  • Launched 3 days ago

Steps

  1. Brown the butter until it’s golden and nutty, typically 5–10 minutes over medium heat. Then add the coconut sugar and whisk until fully cover in butter. Carefully add the water while whisking.
  2. Add the allulose and stir until both sugars are dissolved.
  3. Next, add the cinnamon sticks, cloves ginger, nutmeg and molasses. Simmer gently for 10ish minutes.
  4. Remove from heat and let it cool for about 10 minutes. Add vanilla bean paste and butter extract. Allow to steep with the spices for 30-60 minutes. Before storing, remove the cinnamon sticks and cloves.
  5. I start with 30g of syrup in a double shot iced latte. Adjust from there depending on how sweet you want it. My picky husband like it a bit sweeter (closer to 40g). It gives you that warm, spiced cookie flavor without needing a ton of syrup.
  6. Store it in a sealed jar or bottle in the fridge. Give it a good shake before using since we’re working with real browned butter here.
