How to Make the Perfectly Flaky and Buttery Homemade Pie Crust

Serves 2

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • YIELD: 9 inch (23 cm) pie crust
  • 1 1/2 cups (185 gr) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons (25 gr) sugar
  • 4 oz (115 GR) unsalted butter, cold
  • about 5 to 6 tablespoons ice cold water

Steps

  1. In your food processor, add the flour, salt and sugar. Pulse a couple of times so that the dry ingredients are mixed together. If not using a food processor, combine all the dry ingredients in a bowl.
  2. Add the cubed butter and pulse a few times until incorporated. You need the butter in little pea-size small clumps. If not using a food processor, cut the butter in small pieces with the tip of a knife, mixing with the flour, until you get a coarse mixture.
  3. Add about 4 tablespoons of chilled water. I placed half glass of water in the freezer before starting with the recipe. Pulse only a few times, (or mix with a spoon if not using a food processor) and check the dough. You need to stop as soon as the dough comes together in a ball. Do not over-mix. Add a little more water if necessary. I added two more tablespoons of water (total of 6).
  4. Pack the dough into a disc using your hand and wrap in plastic wrap. Refrigerate for one hour or longer. You can prepare the dough the day before too, and leave it in the refrigerator overnight.
  5. Roll the dough on a clean surface sprinkled with flour, into a circle of about 12 inches (30 cm) in diameter. Make sure the dough doesn't stick to the counter when you roll it, so flip it and move it around.
  6. Transfer the dough to a 9 inches pie pan, helping yourself with the rolling pin. Cover the pan with the dough pushing gently the dough down to the bottom, without stretching it. Trim off the excess pastry around the edges, leaving about one inch all around.
  7. Fold back the edge, toward the outside of the pan, And if you like, make a fluted edge. Using your finger index on one hand, push the dough through the index and middle fingers of your other hand, as shown in my picture.
  8. Prick the bottom of the crust with a fork Store in the refrigerator while preparing the filling!

Naturally Leavened Bread

Serves 2

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 250 grams active starter
  • 725 grams warm filtered water
  • 25 grams salt
  • 1,000 grams unbleached all-purpose flour

Steps

  1. You'll need an active bubbly starter at its peak on a digital scale.
  2. Place your bowl on the scale and zero it out.
  3. Add 250 grams of active starter.
  4. Zero out your scale again and add 725 grams of warm filtered water.
  5. Remove the bowl from the scale and mix the starter and water together.
  6. Put the bowl back on the scale and zero it out.
  7. Add 25 grams of salt.
  8. Zero out your scale again and add 1,000 grams of unbleached all-purpose flour.
  9. Mix until there are no bits of flour left and it turns into a shaggy dough.
  10. Scrape down the sides of the bowl and cover it with a plate or kitchen towel.
  11. Let it sit on the counter for one hour.
  12. After an hour, perform the first round of stretch and folds by pulling up one side of the dough and folding it over.
  13. Repeat this process around the bowl about 10 times.
  14. Cover the dough and let it rest for another 30 minutes.
  15. After 30 minutes, perform the second round of stretch and folds.
  16. Cover the dough and let it rest for another 30 minutes.
  17. After another 30 minutes, perform the third round of stretch and folds.
  18. Cover the dough and let it rest for another 30 minutes.
  19. After the final 30 minutes, perform the fourth round of stretch and folds.
  20. Cover the dough and let it bulk ferment for about two hours.
  21. Once the dough has risen significantly, add flour to your surface and pour the dough onto it.
  22. Cut the dough in half to shape two loaves.
  23. For the first shape, stretch the dough, fold it over, roll it up, and shape it into a round ball.
  24. Let it rest on the counter for 20 minutes.
  25. For the final shape, flip the dough over, stretch it gently, fold it, and roll it into a round ball again.
  26. Flip it into a banneton and cover it with a kitchen towel.
  27. Place it in the fridge to proof for two hours.
  28. After two hours, flip the dough onto parchment paper and score it.
  29. Preheat your Dutch ovens to 500 degrees and place them in the oven for 20 minutes.
  30. Bake at 500 degrees for 35 minutes, then remove the tops and bake for an additional 10 minutes at 425 degrees.
  31. Enjoy your beautiful, crispy naturally leavened bread.

  • baking powder
  • baking soda
  • sour cream
  • milk
  • powdered sugar

Steps

  1. Make the crumb topping by combining melted butter, brown sugar, flour, cinnamon, and salt until it forms a thick mixture. Set aside.
  2. Place a whisk attachment onto your stand mixer.

  6. In a separate bowl, mix all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until combined.
  7. Alternate adding half the dry ingredients to the wet mixture, then add sour cream and milk, mixing until combined.
  8. Add the remaining dry ingredients and mix until just incorporated.
  9. Pour the batter into a parchment lined 8 by 8 pan and spread it to the edges.
  10. Take the crumb topping and squeeze it between your palms over the batter, breaking it into chunks.
  11. Gently pat the crumb topping to help it settle into the cake.
  12. Bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for about 35 minutes until golden brown and a knife comes out clean.
  13. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1/3 cup (65 g) olive oil
  • 2/3 cup (170 g) creamy almond butter
  • 1 1/4 cup (200 g) coconut sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 2 tsp (10 g) vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) almond flour, packed
  • 2 cups (170 g) gluten free rolled oats
  • 1 tsp (6 g) baking soda
  • 1/2 tsp (3 g) salt
  • 1 1/2 cup (250 g) dark chocolate chips or chunks
  • Flaky sea salt

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Add olive oil, almond butter, coconut sugar, eggs and vanilla extract to a bowl and mix well.
  2. Mix in flour, oats, baking soda and salt until fully incorporated then fold in chocolate chunks.
  3. Spread cookie dough in an even layer in a 9x9 greased or parchment lined baking dish, then top with extra chocolate chunks, if desired.
  4. Bake for 40-45 minutes until the center is set and the edges are crispy.
  5. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt and allow bars to cool before slicing.

Dad

Ingredients

  • For the Chicken:
  • 1 1/2 lbs (680 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs
  • Seasoning: 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tbsp onion powder, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp allspice, 2 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp pepper, 1 tsp salt
  • 3 tbsp olive oil 8 garlic cloves
  • 1/2 lemon, juiced
  • -2 tsp @betterthanbouillon roasted chicken base
  • For the Rice:
  • 3 tbsp butter 1 1/2 cups yellow onion, diced
  • 1 tbsp turmeric, 2 tsp paprika, 2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tsp pepper
  • 1 1/2 cups basmati rice
  • 3 cups hot water
  • -3 tsp @betterthanbouillon roasted chicken base
  • For the Fresh Sumac Salad:
  • 1/2 large red onion, thinly sliced
  • 1 cup cherry tomatoes, quartered
  • 1 cup cucumber, sliced then halved
  • 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper & 2 tsp sumac
  • 1/2 lemon, juiced
  • For the Garlic Sauce:
  • 1/4 cup mayonnaise 1/4 cup plain Greek yogurt
  • 2 to 3 garlic cloves 1 tbsp fresh parsley
  • 1 tsp salt 1 tsp black pepper
  • 1/2 lemon, juiced 1 tbsp olive oil

Steps

  1. In a bowl, combine the chicken with the spices, olive oil, garlic, lemon juice and Better Than Bouillon. Mix well. Marinate for as long as your patience can handle.
  2. Heat a large pan over medium-high heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken in batches. Cook for 6 to 8 mins per side until golden and cooked through. Set aside.
  3. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add butter to the same pan then the onions & cook, stirring often, until translucent. Add the garlic & spices, cook for 1 to 2 mins. Add the rice and toast for 2 mins while stirring. Pour in the hot water mixed with Better Than Bouillon. Stir & bring to a boil. Once boiling, cover & reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 mins until cooked.
  4. Mix the salad ingredients in one bowl and the sauce ingredients in another bowl. Enjoy!

Dad

Ingredients

  • Parchment paper
  • 1 1/2 cups of sugar
  • 7 tablespoons of milk
  • 2 tablespoons of shortening
  • 1/4 teaspoon of salt
  • 2 tablespoons of margarine
  • 1/2 cup of creamy peanut butter
  • 1 teaspoon of vanilla

Steps

  1. Prepare a box of brownies according to the package directions, using an 8 by 8 pan or double the recipe for a 9 by 13 pan.
  2. Line the pan with parchment paper for easy removal after baking.
  3. Mix 1 and 1/2 cups of sugar, 7 tablespoons of milk, 2 tablespoons of shortening, and 1/4 teaspoon of salt in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
  4. Add 2 tablespoons of margarine and mix until melted and combined.
  5. Allow the mixture to come to a boil, then set a timer for 2 minutes without stirring.
  6. After 2 minutes, turn off the heat and add 1/2 cup of creamy peanut butter and 1 teaspoon of vanilla, stirring to combine.
  7. Pour the peanut butter fudge over the brownies in the pan and let it sit on the counter for about 1 to 2 hours to cool before cutting.
  8. Once cooled, lift the brownies out of the pan using the parchment paper and cut into desired sizes.

Peanut Butter Oreo Pie

Serves 8

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1 package of Oreos
  • 1 stick of butter
  • 2 blocks of softened cream cheese
  • 2 cups of powdered sugar
  • 2 cups of creamy peanut butter
  • 16 ounce container of Cool Whip
  • mini Oreos
  • Reese's
  • 1/4 cup of peanut butter

Steps

  1. Grab a 9 by 13 pan and a package of Oreos.
  2. Crush the Oreos as finely as possible using hands and a rolling pin or a food processor.
  3. Dump the crushed Oreos into the No. 13 pan.
  4. Melt one stick of butter and pour it into the crushed Oreos, mixing well.
  5. Press the mixture down with a spatula and place it in the freezer.
  6. In a large bowl, add two blocks of softened cream cheese, two cups of powdered sugar, and two cups of creamy peanut butter.
  7. Use an electric mixer to mix the ingredients well.
  8. Grab a 16 ounce container of Cool Whip and fold half of it into the peanut butter mixture.
  9. Remove the Oreo crust from the freezer and scoop the peanut butter mixture on top, smoothing it out.
  10. Add the rest of the Cool Whip on top of the peanut butter mixture.
  11. Heat around a fourth of a cup of peanut butter in the microwave for 30 seconds to a minute until runny.
  12. Top the pie with mini Oreos and chopped Reese's, then drizzle the heated peanut butter on top.
  13. Let the pie sit in the refrigerator for a couple of hours before serving.

Peanut Butter Pie

Serves 8

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • entire package Reese's Oreos
  • 5 tablespoons melted butter
  • 2 blocks (8 ounce each) cream cheese
  • 3 cups creamy peanut butter
  • 2 capfuls vanilla extract
  • 2/3 cup powdered sugar
  • 1 1/2 cups heavy cream
  • 3/4 cup heavy cream (for ganache)
  • 8 ounces Hershey's milk chocolate chips

Steps

  1. Crush the entire package of Reese's Oreos in a blender until fine crumbs.
  2. Mix the Oreo crumbs with 5 tablespoons melted butter and press the mixture into the bottom of a springform pan; chill to harden.
  3. In a mixer, combine the two 8‑ounce blocks of cream cheese, 3 cups peanut butter, vanilla, powdered sugar, and 1.5 cups heavy cream; mix until smooth.
  4. Spread the peanut butter filling over the chilled crust and smooth the top; freeze for about 15 minutes.
  5. Heat 3/4 cup heavy cream in a saucepan until it just begins to simmer, then remove from heat.
  6. Stir in 8 ounces milk chocolate chips until the ganache is smooth.
  7. Pour the chocolate ganache over the frozen filling and smooth the surface.
  8. Refrigerate the pie for several hours until set before serving.

Perfect Brownie Recipe

Serves 2

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 10 tablespoons butter
  • 1 1/4 cups light brown sugar
  • 3/4 cup flour
  • 1/2 cup cocoa powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup chocolate chips

Steps

  1. Start by measuring 10 tablespoons of butter and 1 and a quarter cups of light brown sugar, packing the brown sugar tightly.
  2. Microwave the butter and brown sugar mixture for 2 minutes, stirring every 30 seconds until it becomes a glossy mixture.
  3. Add eggs directly from the fridge to the hot mixture and stir immediately.
  4. Switch to an electric mixer and mix for about 45 seconds.
  5. In a separate bowl, combine 3 quarters of a cup of flour, a half cup of cocoa powder, half a teaspoon of salt, and a teaspoon of vanilla extract.
  6. Mix the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just combined.
  7. Fold in half a cup of chocolate chips.
  8. Pour the batter into a preheated 350-degree oven and bake for about 25 minutes.
  9. Once baked, let the brownies cool before cutting into them. Enjoy!

  • Wet ingredients

  • 1 cup pumpkin puree
  • 1/4 cup avocado oil, or any neutral oil

  • 1/4 cup milk
  • 2 eggs
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • Dry ingredients
  • 5/3 cup white whole wheat flour
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • 1 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice
  • 1 tsp cinnamon
  • 1/4 tsp salt
  • 1/2 cup mini chocolate chips, optional, more for topping

Steps

  1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F, arrange rack to middle position.
  2. Prepare a 12-muffin pan with muffin liners.
  3. Add all dry ingredients (except chocolate chips) to a large bowl. Whisk to combine and set aside.
  4. In a high speed blender add cottage cheese, milk, oil, honey, eggs and vanilla. Blend until smooth.
  5. Pour wet ingredients into the large bowl with dry ingredients and combine. Use a rubber spatula to make sure you get all of the batter out of the blender.
  6. Fold in chocolate chips if desired.
  7. Divide muffin batter evenly into prepared tins and top with extra chocolate chips. If you're leaving out chocolate chips, sprinkle with turbinado sugar and cinnamon before baking.
  8. Bake for 18-20 minutes or until the tops are golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the muffin comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes in the pan before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

Queen Ina Gardens Giant Crinkle Cookie

Serves 8

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 2 sticks butter
  • 1/4 cup light brown sugar
  • 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
  • 1 extra large egg
  • 1 tablespoon vanilla extract
  • 2 tablespoons water
  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 3 bars chocolate, chopped

Steps

  1. Soften the butter quickly in the microwave.
  2. Cream the softened butter with the brown sugar and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
  3. Add the egg, vanilla, and water to the butter‑sugar mixture and continue to cream for another 3 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
  4. In a separate bowl combine the flour, baking soda, and salt; then gradually add to the wet mixture, mixing just until incorporated.
  5. Fold in the chopped chocolate bars, being careful not to over‑mix.
  6. Scoop the dough into large 2½‑inch balls and place on a baking sheet; freeze for exactly 15 minutes.
  7. Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
  8. Bake the frozen dough balls for 10 minutes, then remove and “slam” (press) each cookie to create a crackled surface.
  9. Return the cookies to the oven and bake for an additional 3 minutes.
  10. Repeat the slamming and baking steps once more for extra texture, then allow cookies to cool.

Same Day Sourdough Sandwich Bread

Serves 2

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 125 grams active starter
  • 325 grams warm filtered water
  • 12 grams extra virgin olive oil
  • 12 grams honey (or 12 grams sugar as a substitute)
  • 500 grams unbleached flour (all-purpose or bread flour)
  • 12 grams salt

Steps

  1. Grab a bowl and a digital scale.
  2. Start with 125 grams of active bubbly starter.
  3. Add 325 grams of warm filtered water and mix until most of the starter is dissolved.
  4. Zero out your scale and add 12 grams of extra virgin olive oil.
  5. Zero out your scale again and add 12 grams of honey (or sugar if preferred).
  6. Zero out your scale once more and add 500 grams of unbleached flour.
  7. Zero out your scale again and add 12 grams of salt.
  8. Mix the dough by hand until it comes together and has a consistent feel, about three minutes.
  9. Scrape down the sides of the bowl to gather all the dough in the middle.
  10. Cover the bowl with a kitchen towel and let it rest for 30 minutes.
  11. After 30 minutes, perform the first set of stretching folds by pulling one side of the dough up and folding it over the middle. Repeat this around the bowl four times.
  12. Cover the bowl and let it rest for another 30 minutes.
  13. Repeat the stretching folds for the second set, covering the bowl afterward and resting for another 30 minutes.
  14. Perform the third set of stretching folds, cover the bowl, and let it rest for another 30 minutes.
  15. For the final set of stretching folds, cover the bowl again and let it rise at room temperature for about three to four hours, until it is almost doubled in size.
  16. Once the dough has risen, pour it out onto a floured counter and shape it into a rectangle, popping any air bubbles.
  17. Fold the sides of the rectangle into the middle, then roll it up tightly from one end.
  18. Tuck the ends under to seal and create tension in the loaf using a bench scraper or your hands.
  19. Place the seam side down in a greased 9 by 5 loaf pan.
  20. Cover and let it proof at room temperature for two hours, or until it fills the pan and rises slightly above the edge.
  21. Preheat your oven to 375 degrees.
  22. Once proofed, bake the loaf for about 35 minutes, until golden brown.
  23. After baking, rub the top with butter and let it cool for about 30 minutes before slicing.

Sourdough Chocolate Chip Cookies Recipe - Little Spoon Farm

Serves 12

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • Dry Ingredients
  • 3/4 cup 1 teaspoon (95 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup 1 teaspoon (125 g) bread flour all-purpose can be substituted, see notes
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) fine sea salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
  • Wet Ingredients 1
  • 1 large (1) egg
  • 1/2 cup (125 g) sourdough starter discard
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) vanilla extract
  • Wet Ingredients 2
  • 8 tablespoons (113 g) unsalted butter cold, cubed
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) light brown sugar
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) white granulated sugar
  • 1 1/2 cups (340 g) chocolate chips semi-sweet or milk chocolate

Steps

  1. Mix dry ingredients
  2. Use a whisk or a fork to mix the bread flour, all-purpose flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt in a small bowl. Set aside.
  3. Mix wet ingredients 1
  4. In a separate small bowl, use a whisk or a fork to beat the egg, vanilla extract and sourdough starter until smooth. Set aside.
  5. Mix wet ingredients 2
  6. Place the cold, cubed butter, light brown sugar and granulated sugar into the bowl of a stand mixer with the paddle attachment. Beat on low-speed until the mixture forms small crumbles, 45-60 seconds. Add the chocolate chips and mix on low-speed 30-45 seconds. Scrape down the sides of the bowl.
  7. Add the dry ingredients and mix on low-speed until the batter starts to become a crumbly mixture, 20-30 seconds. Pour in the egg mixture and mix on low-speed until the dough comes together and starts to pull away from the sides of the bowl, 20-30 seconds. Use a spatula to stir the batter, ensuring all of the ingredients have been fully incorporated.
  8. Use a cookie scoop to portion the dough into 12 balls, (2 scoops per cookie) and place them on a parchment-lined baking tray. Cover the dough with a sheet of plastic wrap so they do not dry out. Chill the dough in the fridge for a minimum of 2 hours. (24 hours is best!)
  9. Bake in a preheated, 375°F (190°C) oven for 15-17 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the center still appears slightly under-baked. Remove and allow the cookies to rest on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring them to a cooling rack.

Sourdough Discard Hawaiian Rolls

Serves 15

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • For the Dough
  • 1/2 cup canned pineapple juice room temperature
  • 1/4 cup non-dairy or regular dairy milk warmed to 110
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons instant yeast
  • 1/4 cup light brown sugar packed
  • 3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 200 grams (about 3/4 cup) sourdough discard unfed, at room temperature
  • 1 egg lightly beaten
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 3 Tablespoons unsalted butter divided and melted
  • For Topping
  • 1 egg beaten with 1 Tablespoon water for egg wash
  • 1 Tablespoon unsalted butter (optional) melted

Steps

  1. Combine the pineapple juice, milk, instant yeast and brown sugar in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook*. Add the flour, sourdough discard, beaten egg, vanilla extract and salt. With the mixer on low, slowly pour in 2 Tablespoons of melted butter. Increase speed to medium and mix until a shaggy dough forms, about 2 minutes.
  2. Transfer the dough to a smooth work surface and knead until smooth, about 3-4 minutes. The dough should be smooth, soft and just slightly tacky (not sticky). If needed, add more flour or milk (1 Tablespoon at a time) to reach your desired consistency.
  3. Transfer the dough to a large oiled bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Let rise for 90 minutes, or until doubled in size.
  4. Brush a 9x13-inch baking pan with the remaining 1 Tablespoon of melted butter and set aside.
  5. Turn the dough onto a smooth work surface and divide into 15 equal-sized pieces. This doesn't have to be exact, but if you do want perfectly identical rolls, weigh the dough on a kitchen scale and divide that number by 15. For me, each roll weighs about 73 grams.Using your palm for friction, roll each piece of dough into a ball, then place the rolls into the prepared baking pan with the seam-side down. Repeat until you have 15 rolls.
  6. Cover the baking pan with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let the rolls rise for 60 minutes until puffed and doubled in size.
  7. Preheat the oven to 375℉. Lightly brush the rolls with egg wash. Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown. Let cool slightly in the pan, then brush with 1 Tablespoon melted butter before serving (optional).

Sourdough Pizza Dough

Serves 2

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 150 g active starter
  • 300 g water
  • 500 g flour
  • 15 g olive oil
  • 15 g salt

Steps

  1. Starting off with 150 grams of sourdough starter.
  2. Add 300 grams of room temperature filtered water.
  3. Add 15 grams of olive oil.
  4. Add 500 grams total of flour (50 grams of whole wheat and 450 grams of bread flour).
  5. Add 15 grams of salt.
  6. Mix the dough until it has a nice shaggy consistency with no dry flour left in the bowl.
  7. Cover the dough and leave it for an hour.
  8. After an hour, perform a gentle round of stretch and folds.
  9. Cover the dough and leave it for another hour.
  10. After the second hour, perform another round of stretch and folds.
  11. Cover the dough and leave it for another hour.
  12. Skip the third round of stretch and folds if the dough is holding together well.
  13. Leave the dough on the counter for a couple of hours to finish its bulk fermentation.
  14. Once bulk fermentation is complete, divide the dough into four equal pieces (about 250 grams each).
  15. Shape each piece into a tight little pizza ball by pulling the edges under and turning it.
  16. Place the shaped dough into an airtight container.
  17. Refrigerate the dough to use within the next five days.

  5. In a separate bowl, combine low sodium soy sauce, brown sugar, honey, red pepper flakes, minced garlic, water, ground ginger, and oyster sauce.
  6. Whisk the sauce mixture together until well combined.
  7. Add the beef ribs to the crock pot.
  8. Pour the sauce mixture over the beef ribs and cover the crock pot.
  9. Cook on low for eight hours.
  10. Once cooked, carefully remove the ribs from the crock pot as they will be very tender.
  11. In a bowl, whisk together two tablespoons of water and two tablespoons of cornstarch.
  12. Add the cornstarch mixture into the sauce in the crock pot and whisk until the sauce thickens.
  13. Pour the thickened sauce over the ribs.
  14. Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.

Tex-Mex Beef Enchiladas

Serves 8

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • For the Beef
  • 2 lbs ground beef
  • 1 yellow onion, diced
  • 1–2 tbsp minced garlic
  • 1 tsp onion powder
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 tsp tomato chicken bouillon
  • 1 packet Sazón, optional
  • Pinch of black pepper
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 1/2 cup water
  • For the Enchilada Sauce
  • 4 tbsp butter
  • 4 tbsp all-purpose flour
  • 3 cups beef broth, more or less depending on your preferred sauce thickness
  • 2 tbsp chili powder
  • 1/2 tsp paprika
  • 1/2 tsp garlic powder
  • 1/2 tsp onion powder
  • Salt to taste, starting with 1/2 tsp
  • For Assembly
  • About 20 corn tortillas
  • Oil, for lightly frying the tortillas
  • Shredded Mexican-blend cheese, as needed

Steps

  1. Add the ground beef and diced onion to a large skillet over medium heat. Cook until the beef is browned and the onion is tender. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute. Drain the excess grease.
  2. Season the beef with onion powder, garlic powder, tomato chicken bouillon, Sazón, if using, and a pinch of black pepper. Stir in the tomato paste and ½ cup water. Cook for a few minutes, stirring until everything is well combined and the beef mixture has thickened slightly. Set aside.
  3. Add a thin layer of oil to a skillet over medium heat. Sauté each corn tortilla for about 10 seconds per side. You only want to soften them. You don't want them crispy. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining tortillas. Trust me, this step is a MUST! Once finished, remove the oil from the pan.
  4. Melt the butter in a skillet or saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for about 1 minute.
  5. Slowly pour in the beef broth while whisking to prevent lumps. Start with less broth and add more as needed until the sauce reaches your preferred consistency.
  6. Add the chili powder, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and salt. Continue cooking and whisking until the sauce is smooth and slightly thickened. Taste and adjust the salt if needed.
  7. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Spread enough enchilada sauce across the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish to completely cover it.
  8. Dip a prepared corn tortilla into the enchilada sauce, coating both sides. Place it in the baking dish and add some of the ground beef mixture and shredded Mexican-blend cheese. Roll the tortilla and place it seam-side down.
  9. Repeat with the remaining tortillas until your baking dish is full. Depending on how tightly they're rolled, a 9x13-inch dish should hold around 12 enchiladas. The full recipe makes approximately 20 enchiladas, so you may need a second baking dish.
  10. Spoon additional ground beef over the enchiladas, pour more enchilada sauce over the top, and finish with plenty of shredded cheese.
  11. Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes, or until the enchiladas are hot and bubbly and the cheese is completely melted.
  12. Serve warm with your favorite toppings like sour cream, cilantro, diced tomatoes, avocado, or jalapeños.

The BEST Brookies

Serves 12

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • Cookie Dough
  • 3/4 cup (168 g) unsalted butter, melted (can be warm but not hot)
  • 3/4 cup (150 g) light brown sugar, packed
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 tbsp vanilla extract
  • 1/2 tsp baking powder
  • 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  • 1 tbsp cornstarch
  • 2 cups (256 g) all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled
  • 1 1/2 cups semisweet chocolate chips, divided (I do half mini half reg)
  • Flaky sea salt, for sprinkling on top
  • Brownie Batter
  • 1/2 cup (112 g) unsalted butter, sliced
  • 1/4 cup (54 g) refined coconut oil
  • 3/4 cup (75 g) regular unsweetened cocoa powder
  • 3/4 cup (120 g) dark chocolate chips
  • 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) light brown sugar, packed
  • 3 large eggs
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1/2 tsp kosher salt
  • 1/2 cup (65 g) all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled

Steps

  1. Cookie Dough:
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the butter, brown sugar, and sugar until well combined.
  3. Vigorously whisk in the egg and vanilla for a good minute or until the mixture turns creamy and a shade lighter.
  4. Whisk in the baking powder, salt, and cornstarch to evenly incorporate.
  5. Switch to a rubber spatula and fold in the flour. About halfway through, add in 1 cup of chocolate chips and fold to fully bring the dough together. It will be thick and sticky.
  6. Place in the refrigerator uncovered.
  7. Brownie:
  8. Add the butter and coconut oil to a medium saucepan and stir to melt over medium heat.
  9. Once melted and hot, whisk in the cocoa powder and allow to bubble for about 30 seconds. Remove from heat and whisk in the chocolate chips until smooth. Set aside.
  10. In a separate large bowl, vigorously whisk together the sugar, brown sugar, and eggs for a good minute or until creamy and a shade lighter.
  11. Whisk in the vanilla and salt, followed by the chocolate mixture.
  12. Add in the flour and whisk just to combine.
  13. Grease and line a 9×13 baking pan with parchment paper, allowing some paper to hang over the sides for easy removal.
  14. Spread the batter in the pan and place in the refrigerator to chill for 15 minutes. In the meantime, preheat the oven to 350F.
  15. Once the brownie batter is chilled and feels firmer to the touch, it’s time to add the cookie dough on top.
  16. Take spoonfuls of the chilled dough and press flat between your hands. Lay on top of the brownie layer to cover the surface in patches of cookie dough. Near the end, use any remaining dough to fill in the gaps to fully cover the surface.
  17. Top with the remaining 1/2 cup of chocolate chips and gently press into the surface.
  18. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes or until the bars are evenly puffed and lightly golden on the surface.
  19. Drop the pan a couple times right when it’s fresh from the oven to deflate the bars. Then sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
  20. Allow to cool for about 20 minutes at room temperature, then transfer to the refrigerator to chill for an hour or until just barely warm.
  21. Once cooled, lift out of the pan and slice into 12 large squares or 24 smaller squares. I suggest running a knife under the bars to help release from the paper. Enjoy!

The Best Chocolate Chip Cookie

Ingredients

  • 1 stick unsalted butter
  • 3 ice cubes
  • 150 grams brown sugar
  • 1 egg
  • 1/2 tablespoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 100 grams ground oats
  • 120 grams all-purpose flour
  • 170 grams chocolate chips

Steps

  1. Brown one stick of unsalted butter until it is a little darker than light brown and then kill the heat.
  2. Add three ice cubes to the browned butter to add back moisture and cool it down.
  3. Stir in 150 grams (3/4 cup) of brown sugar until combined.
  4. Add one egg and half a tablespoon of vanilla extract, then stir until it forms a thick batter.
  5. Mix in 1/2 teaspoon each of baking powder, baking soda, and kosher salt.
  6. Grind 100 grams of whole oats until powdery, then add to the mixture.
  7. Stir in 120 grams (1 cup) of all-purpose flour until combined.
  8. Add 170 grams (about 1 cup) of chocolate chips and stir until the dough is well mixed.
  9. Scoop the dough using a No. 20 scoop (about 3 tablespoons) and place on a baking sheet.
  10. Refrigerate the cookie dough for about 24 hours to let it age.
  11. Bake at 350°F for about 10 minutes for fresh dough, or at 280°F for about 26 minutes for frozen dough.

The BEST Mexican Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowls — Jazz Leaf

Serves 4

Family ratings

Mom
Dad
Kids

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
  • 2 tablespoons taco seasoning, divided
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 1/2 cups frozen corn
  • 3 tablespoons plain Greek yogurt
  • 3 tablespoons mayo
  • 2 tablespoons lime juice
  • 1/2 cup pico de gallo
  • 1 avocado, sliced
  • Fresh cilantro and hot sauce to garnish (optional)
  • 2 pouches cilantro lime microwavable rice OR fresh rice. See bottom for instructions on that
  • Cilantro Lime Rice Ingredients
  • 2 cups basmati rice
  • 4 cups cold water
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon avocado oil
  • 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
  • 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, roughly chopped

Steps

  1. Toss the cubed chicken breast with 1.5 tablespoons of taco seasoning until evenly coated.
  2. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through (internal temp 165 degrees F). Remove from the pan and set aside.
  3. Without wiping the pan, add the frozen corn and remaining half tablespoon of taco seasoning directly to the same skillet. Cook over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, letting the corn sit without stirring so it picks up a light char and absorbs the seasoning left from the chicken. Remove from heat and stir in the pico de gallo. The residual heat from the corn will slightly soften the pico without cooking it down completely.
  4. While the corn cooks, whisk together the Greek yogurt, mayo, and lime juice in a small bowl until smooth.
  5. Pour ½ of the lime crema into the corn and pico mixture and mix to combine. Reserve some of the sauce over the top of the bowls.
  6. Microwave the rice pouches according to package directions.
  7. Divide the rice between four bowls. Top with corn and pico, cooked chicken, and avocado slices. Spoon the lime lime crema, and finish with sliced avocado, fresh cilantro, lime juice and hot sauce if using.
  8. Cilantro Lime Rice:
  9. Rinse the rice under cold water 6 to 8 times until the water runs clear. Add the rinsed rice to a non-stick saucepan with the 4 cups of cold water, salt, and avocado oil. Stir to combine.
  10. Place over medium-high heat and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and let the rice simmer for 10 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
  11. Remove from heat and let it sit covered for 2 minutes. Fluff with a fork, then immediately stir in the lime juice and fresh cilantro. Taste and adjust with more lime or salt if needed.
  12. Do not crowd the pan when cooking the chicken. Cook in two batches if needed so the chicken sears rather than steams.
  13. Use high heat for the corn and resist stirring constantly. The char is where the elote flavor comes from.
  14. The crema ratio is a starting point. Go up to 4 or 5 tablespoons of each if you want a saucier bowl.
  15. Rotisserie chicken is a great shortcut. Warm it in the skillet with the taco seasoning and skip the full cook step. Total time drops to about 15 minutes.
  16. Store all components separately in airtight containers for up to 4 days. Add avocado and pico fresh when serving.

  1. First, the cottage cheese. I processed 8oz cottage cheese in a small food processor until smooth to get rid of the curds. Transfer to a small oven-safe bowl.
  2. To the processed cottage cheese, crack in 2 eggs
  3. Add the cacao powder (I use 3 tbsp … sometimes more… but I like it really rich)
  4. Stir in 3 to 4 tbsp of powdered monkfruit or preferred sweetener. Make sure it’s POWDERED. That is key
  5. Add a splash of vanilla extract and mix thoroughly till you have a nice smooth batter.
  6. Sprinkle chocolate chips on top, if desired, shake it so it somewhat submerges into the cake to get you the lava cake feel. Again, use as many as you like
  7. Pop it into the oven and bake at 350°F for 33-35 mins.
  8. Remove, let cool for two or three mins.
